Aloud gives audibility: the inner state of grief, thanksgiving or distress, named by another word of the verse, is voiced so that it is heard.

Being silent is a person's, or God's, holding back of speech for a reason the verse shows: submission, fear, shame, awe, wisdom, obedience, waiting, or failure to speak up; or the refusal of it (anguish, praise, the watchmen's duty).
Call is a purposeful act of the inner being turned to God: calling or crying out to the Lord, or on his name, in need, trust, praise or worship, or refusing to.
Call is here the outward use of the Lord's name over others (a formula spoken over a person or thing); it is the outward act and bears on them, with no inner operation of the speaker named.
Call here only names, designates or labels a person, place or thing (to be called such a name, to call it so); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.
Called is here the outward act of summoning, addressing or sending for another person or thing; it bears on the other's response but names no inner-being operation of the one who calls.
Call, in a naming, voices the inner state of the one who names, stated in the verse (grief, hope, thanks, trust or confession): the name is a purposeful act of the heart made audible.
New here describes a thing, a time or a figure (a new garment, a new cart, fresh water, an old pool, a parable of wineskins); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.
Old is here the former time (the days of old, the things of old) as what remembering, considering or comfort is directed at; the inner act is named by another word of the verse.
Angry is here the anger, wrath, rage or fury of a person or people: a state of the heart aroused against another, a thing or God, named by the word itself.

Angry is here the anger, wrath or fury of God against persons or nations (kindled, poured out, turned away, executed, provoked); it is God's own act upon them, and bears on their inner response, which other words of the verse name, if at all.
Vexation is here vexation, grief or sullen distress of the heart: an inner state of irritation or sorrow, named by the word itself.
Consecrated is here the act of consecrating oneself or one's heart to the Lord: a purposeful act of the person's will, dedicated to God.

Godliness is here the godliness, devoutness, reverence or uprightness of a person as a state of the heart toward God or toward what is right (a devout man who feared God, godliness trained and pursued, uprightness of heart, reverence and awe).

Holy here names an attribute of God or of his rule (a righteous Lord, the scepter of uprightness, the Holy One, his holy name or Spirit, the mystery of godliness); no operation of a person's inner being is voiced by it.

Holy is here the godliness, devoutness, reverence or uprightness of a person as a state of the heart toward God or toward what is right (a devout man who feared God, godliness trained and pursued, uprightness of heart, reverence and awe).

Righteous is here the godliness, devoutness, reverence or uprightness of a person as a state of the heart toward God or toward what is right (a devout man who feared God, godliness trained and pursued, uprightness of heart, reverence and awe).

Righteous is here the godly, the righteous, the upright, the wicked or the ungodly as a class of persons toward whom an act is directed or whom an event befalls (the Lord keeps the godly, do not envy the wicked, Christ died for the ungodly); the act is named by another word of the verse.

Righteousness is here the godliness, devoutness, reverence or uprightness of a person as a state of the heart toward God or toward what is right (a devout man who feared God, godliness trained and pursued, uprightness of heart, reverence and awe).

Upright is here the godliness, devoutness, reverence or uprightness of a person as a state of the heart toward God or toward what is right (a devout man who feared God, godliness trained and pursued, uprightness of heart, reverence and awe).

Wicked is here the godly, the righteous, the upright, the wicked or the ungodly as a class of persons toward whom an act is directed or whom an event befalls (the Lord keeps the godly, do not envy the wicked, Christ died for the ungodly); the act is named by another word of the verse.

Wicked gives a moral condition to what it binds (an upright heart, a righteous or wicked way, godly grief, walking uprightly, a sinful nation): the uprightness, godliness or wickedness of the heart, speech, way or conduct.

Wicked is here the wickedness, ungodliness or sinfulness of a person as a state or practice of the heart, set against godliness and what is right (ungodliness, a heart busy with iniquity, a wicked deed, sinful passions).

Wickedness is here the wickedness, ungodliness or sinfulness of a person as a state or practice of the heart, set against godliness and what is right (ungodliness, a heart busy with iniquity, a wicked deed, sinful passions).

Above gives the inner operation or quality it is joined to its priority, its superiority or its origin: love set first before all else, fear of the Lord supreme over the gods, the heart or the self lifted over others, wisdom from above.
Arise here is bodily rising, going or acting, or something coming into being, or God arising; no human inner-being operation is qualified.
Devise names the inner operation of planning, scheming or designing: evil devised in the heart, good devised, and the skill given to devise designs.
Heights here are high places, mountains or hill country; no human inner-being operation is named or qualified.

High gives loftiness to the proud heart and its ways (the high hand, the horn lifted on high, the high door, the nest set on high, the high tree brought low), or places the wise and the known beyond reach (too high for a fool, too high to attain).
Higher here is height in space or rank, or God's thoughts and ways above ours; no human inner-being operation is named or qualified.
Mature gives full growth to the inner life: mature in thinking, the mature who receive wisdom, discernment trained, fruit brought to maturity.
Means here is by no means, by all means, resources (according to their means) or what a word means; no inner-being operation is named or qualified.
Put here is placing, setting, laying, putting on or appointing a thing, a garment, a person or a hook, or putting someone in prison; no inner-being operation is named or qualified.
Put names an act on the inner being: joy put in the heart, a purpose put into hearts, fear put on the nations, and being put to shame; the knife put to the throat of appetite.
Simple gives naivety to the person: the simple believes everything, lacks sense, loves being simple, learns prudence when reproved.
Stir names an act on others minds: to stir you up by way of reminder.
Strange here is foreign gods, foreign speech, foreign teaching or an unfamiliar thing; no human inner-being operation is named or qualified.
Treated here is how a person was dealt with, kindly or shamefully; an outward way of dealing, the inner disposition is named by another word.
Use here is employing a tool, a measure, words, a utensil or an offering, or what is of no use; no inner-being operation is named or qualified.
Weigh names the inner operation of judging what is said: let the others weigh what is said.
Weigh here is weighing silver or goods on a scale; no inner operation.
Weighing names the inner operation of pondering: the Preacher weighing and studying and arranging proverbs.
Weighing here is the weight of a ring, a cloak or hair in shekels; no inner operation.
Weight here is the weight of metal, a measure, a crown, a pillar, or the weight of glory; no inner operation is named or qualified.
Withered here is a plant, a vine, grass, a fig tree or a withered hand; no inner-being operation is named or qualified.
Worst is what the enemies imagine: they imagine the worst for me.
Young here is youth in age, a young man, woman, animal or offspring; a description of age or kind, no inner-being operation is named or qualified.
'find' here only names a physical search or finding, a practical or judicial finding, a record search or reconnaissance; no inner-being operation is voiced by it.
'finds' here only names a physical search or finding, a practical or judicial finding, a record search or reconnaissance; no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

'search' is here a desire or purpose of the will directed to an object (glory, wisdom, peace, a sign, rest, favour, one's own good, or a turning to other gods), good or ill; the direction of the will is what 'search' names.
'search' here only names a physical search or finding, a practical or judicial finding, a record search or reconnaissance; no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

'search' is here the outward search or pursuit through which a purpose is carried out (a hunt for a person, God's search for the lost or for sin, the neglect of such a search); it is the outward act, and the inner intent or care is named by other words or only implied.

'search' is here an act whose object is the inner being (God searching hearts, the spirit searching the innermost parts), or what is found is an inner state of the other (favour, mercy, rest, enjoyment, cheer); it bears on the inner being without being the operation.

'searches' is here an act whose object is the inner being (God searching hearts, the spirit searching the innermost parts), or what is found is an inner state of the other (favour, mercy, rest, enjoyment, cheer); it bears on the inner being without being the operation.
'seek' is here a hostile or purposed intent: the will set to kill, harm, destroy, arrest or lead another astray; the deed is told by the verse's other words, the intent is what 'seek' names.

'seek' is here the seeking of God: the heart or will turned to him (his face, name, word or help), in its different degrees: wholehearted, in distress, resolved, or negated; the seeking is itself the inner operation.

'seeking' is here a desire or purpose of the will directed to an object (glory, wisdom, peace, a sign, rest, favour, one's own good, or a turning to other gods), good or ill; the direction of the will is what 'seeking' names.
'sought' here only names a physical search or finding, a practical or judicial finding, a record search or reconnaissance; no inner-being operation is voiced by it.
'come upon' here names an outward matter (an event arriving, a bodily feature, a being sought); no inner-being operation is voiced or qualified by it.
'looking for' is here an outward search for a person as the end of the search; the person sought is the relational target.

In Num 11:12 and Judg 13:3 harah ('to conceive') is said of a woman's bearing of a child: Moses asks whether he conceived the people and gave them birth, a mother's acts set beside nursing, and the angel tells the barren woman, who has not borne children, that she will conceive and bear a son; conceiving is the beginning of the child.

In Job 15:35, Isa 33:11 and Isa 59:4 harah ('to conceive') is not said of a child: what is conceived is trouble, chaff and mischief, and what is born of it is evil, stubble and iniquity; the verbs of pregnancy and birth are carried over to the devising of harm, the birth being the deed that follows the plan.

In Pro 18:11 the rich man's wealth is called his strong city, a high wall in his imagination: the wall is in what he pictures to himself, not in fact, so maskit ('imagination, figure') names what a man holds in his own mind about his security.

In 1Ti 6:5 nomizo ('to suppose, hold as settled') is the opinion of people whose minds are depraved and who lack the truth, that godliness brings profit; the verse sets it beside the constant friction they cause and traces it to their depraved minds.

In Psa 1:2 hagah ('to meditate', literally to mutter) takes the law of the Lord as its object and day and night as its time: the one whose delight is in that law keeps occupied with it without ceasing, so the word names a continual dwelling on the written law.

In Job 32:6, 32:10 and 32:17 Elihu speaks of declaring his deah ('knowledge, opinion'): in 32:6 he was timid to declare it to the aged, in 32:10 and 32:17 he asks to be heard and will answer with his share; the word is a view he holds and means to set out in speech, not a fact he reports.

In Pro 15:28 the righteous man's heart ponders how to answer him who asks, set against the wicked man's mouth that pours out evil: hagah ('to meditate, mutter') is the thinking that comes before speaking, done in the heart, so the answer is weighed before it is given.

In Dan 4:34 and Dan 4:36 manda ('knowledge, understanding') is what Nebuchadnezzar says returned to him: in 4:34 when he lifted his eyes to heaven, after which he blessed the Most High, and in 4:36 together with the glory of his kingdom, his majesty and splendor; it names the understanding he had lost and now has again.
In Psa 119:52 the psalmist calls to mind the Lord's rules from of old and takes comfort: zakar ('to remember') is the recalling of what the Lord has ordained, and the verse gives its effect, comfort.

In Psa 139:23 the psalmist asks God to search him, to know his heart and to try him and know his thoughts: sarappim ('disquieting thoughts') are what stirs within him, set parallel to the heart, and he asks that God himself test and know it.

In Gen 24:22, Jos 7:21 and Eze 5:1 mishqal ('weight') is a weight: a gold ring of half a shekel and two bracelets of ten shekels (Gen 24:22), a bar of gold of fifty shekels (Jos 7:21) and the balances for weighing the hair in the sign-act of Eze 5:1; in all four it is the weight of a thing, not an act of the mind.

In Mat 1:23 the verb whose usual sense is 'to have, hold' stands in the future active, third singular, and carries 'become pregnant' only through the clause it stands in (the virgin, the bearing of a son that follows); the dictionary sense of the code is possession, not conception.

In Heb 11:11 the noun whose dictionary senses are 'foundation, a casting down' is the first member of a two-noun phrase that the verse gives as conceiving; it names the laying down of seed, and the lexicon itself lists 'conception in the womb' for this verse.

In Heb 11:11 the noun 'seed' stands in the genitive, the second member of the phrase that is rendered to conceive (with the casting down, G2602, in the same unit); here it is the male seed, which the lexicon lists for this verse as semen virile.

In Luk 1:31 the verb is in the future indicative, second person, with 'in your womb' and the bearing of a son after it; its sense here is 'become pregnant', one of the senses the lexicon lists for the code (Lk 1:24, 31, 36; 2:21).

In Jdg 13:5, Jdg 13:7 and Isa 7:14 the feminine adjective 'pregnant' is predicated of a woman and followed by the bearing of a son; the word names the state of being with child, and the ESV renders the announcement with the verb conceive.

In Num 5:28 the Niphal (the passive stem, as the morph HVNq3fs shows) of the verb 'to sow' means to be made pregnant, the sense the lexicon lists for the Niphal; the verse sets it as the result for a woman found clean.

In Psa 51:5 the Piel perfect, third feminine singular, of the verb 'to be hot' means to conceive in the sexual sense (the Piel sense the lexicon lists); its subject is the speaker's mother and its object the speaker, so it names the origin of his life.

In Rom 2:15 the plural noun 'reasonings, thoughts' is the subject of the accusing or excusing that stands beside the conscience; the lexicon lists 'a thought, cogitation' for this verse, and the verse makes the thoughts the voices that judge the person.

In Mar 10:42 the participle of the verb 'to think' is used of those reputed to rule the nations; the sense is 'to be reckoned or held to be', a reputation held by others, and not the thinking of the subject, which is where this occurrence departs from the usual sense.

In Mat 1:20 the aorist participle of the verb 'to reflect on' states Joseph's deliberation over the matter before the angel appears; the lexicon's sense 'to revolve thoroughly in the mind, consider carefully' fits, and the object is the circumstances of Mary's pregnancy.

In Heb 11:11 and Heb 11:26 the verb whose first sense is 'to lead' is used of a judgment reached: Sarah judged the one who promised faithful, Moses counted the reproach of Christ a greater wealth; the sense in both is 'to esteem, count, hold to be', the lexicon's 'to think, consider, count'.

In Rom 4:19 the aorist verb of attentive observation has Abraham's own body as its object; the lexicon's sense 'to observe, consider thoroughly, with intense attention' fits, and the verse sets this looking at the facts beside his unweakened faith.

In Heb 11:19 the verb 'to reckon' is in the aorist middle participle and its object is a clause (that God was able to raise); the sense is to conclude by reckoning, reasoning to a conviction on the ground of God's character.

In Rom 4:19 the negator 'not' is stored in the unit of the surface 'considered' but the ESV verse states no negation of the considering: the 'not' in the verse bears on weakening in faith, and the negator sits beside the word, not on it; adjacency is not scope (LX-01). The occurrence is read as the negator it is, with the reach left to the verse.

In Dan 7:8 the Aramaic verb 'to be' (perfect, first person) is not a word of thinking: it stands with the participle of 'contemplate' (H7920) in the same verse and supplies the continued being-at-it of the looking, 'I was considering'; the dictionary sense 'to be, come to pass' is the helper here.

In 1Ki 10:21, 2Ch 9:20 and Neh 13:13 the Niphal of the verb 'to think, reckon' is passive: silver was not reckoned as anything in Solomon's days, and the men were reckoned reliable; the sense is 'to be accounted', the value or standing others assign.

In Pro 17:28 the Niphal imperfect, third masculine singular, means 'is reckoned' (a fool who is silent is reckoned wise); the standing is assigned from outside the person, by what others observe of his silence.

In Job 1:8, Job 2:3 and Pro 24:32 the noun 'heart' is the object-word of an idiom of setting the heart on something (the verbs set or put in the same verses, H7760K and H7896K), and the ESV renders the idiom as considered; the heart is the seat of the attention directed at Job or at the field.

In Ecc 2:11 the Qal of the verb 'to turn' is followed by the preposition and the objects of the speaker's work: the turning is a turning of attention toward them, and the ESV renders it considered; it is a physical verb used of directing the mind.

In Eze 18:28 the Qal narrative form of the verb 'to see' is the first of two acts (he considered, he turned away from the transgressions); the sense is 'to observe, consider', seeing taken in as grounds for the change of direction.

In Job 1:8 and Job 2:3 the verb 'to set, put' (perfect, second masculine singular) is joined with the noun heart in the same units: the idiom is 'set your heart', and it is what the Lord asks of Satan about Job; the physical verb of placing here directs attention.

In Isa 53:8 the Polel imperfect of the verb 'to muse' is put as a question about the speaker's generation: who gave thought to what happened to him; the sense is 'to reflect upon, take to heart', a deliberate musing that the generation did not do.

In Pro 24:32 the verb 'to set, put' (imperfect, first person) is joined with heart (H3820A, id 1281985 in the same verse): the speaker set his heart on what he saw in the field; it is the placing verb of the attention idiom, not a dictionary sense of thought.

In Dan 7:8 the Aramaic Ithpael participle 'contemplate' is the reflecting act of the speaker at the horns, carried with the helper verb 'to be' (H1934) in the same verse; the sense is attentive consideration.

In Pro 16:20 the Hiphil participle of the verb 'to be prudent' has the word (the instruction) as its object: the one who gives attention with insight to the word finds good; the sense is 'to give heed to with understanding', the lexicon's Hiphil 'to give attention to, consider'.

In Act 17:29 the noun 'thought, design' in the genitive qualifies the image made by art: it is the thinking that devises it; the lexicon lists 'the result of thought, invention, device' for this verse, and the verse sets human devising against the divine being.

In 1Cor 8:2 the connective 'but, now' stands at the head of the clause with the verb 'think' (G1380, id 1484787, same unit); it is the connective that turns from the thought of 8:1 to the person who thinks he knows, and is read for that work (RG-07), not for any thinking.

In 1Cor 8:2 the present verb 'to think' has the infinitive 'to know something' as its content: the thought is a self-estimate of his own knowledge, which the verse then contradicts; the sense is 'to suppose, imagine oneself to', the lexicon's 'think, imagine, suppose'.

In Psa 41:7 the Qal imperfect, third masculine plural, of the verb 'to think, plan' has the worst for the speaker as its object: the sense is 'to devise', the planning of harm by those who whisper together against him, the lexicon's 'to plan, devise'.

In Jos 1:8, Psa 63:6 and Psa 143:5 the verb 'to mutter, meditate' is used of reflection on an object the verse names: the Book of the Law by day and night, God on the bed, God's works of old; the sense is a repeated, quiet musing on that object.

In Psa 38:12 the same verb stands in a clause with speaking of ruin: those who seek the speaker's hurt meditate treachery; the object is deceit and the sense is devising harm, which departs from the musing on the Lord seen in the other three verses.

In Gen 24:63 the Qal infinitive 'to meditate' (the lexicon marks the meaning uncertain) states what Isaac went out to do in the field toward evening; the sense is quiet reflection while walking, set before the sight of the camels.

In Psa 77:6, Psa 77:12, Psa 119:15, 119:23, 119:27, 119:48, 119:78, 119:148 and Psa 145:5 the verb 'to muse' is used of the speaker's reflection on an object the verse names: his song, God's work and deeds, the precepts, statutes, promise and wondrous works; the sense is a deliberate pondering of that object.

In Psa 77:3 the same verb stands after remembering God and before the spirit faints; the lexicon lists 'to complain' for the Qal and the verse sets it with moaning, so it is musing that is a complaint, not a study of a named object.

In Psa 49:3 the noun 'meditation' (construct, with the heart) is set in parallel with the mouth's speech of wisdom; it is the inner musing of the heart, and the verse says its content will be understanding.

In Psa 19:14 the noun 'meditation' (construct, with the heart) is set in parallel with the words of the mouth and both are asked to be acceptable; it is the inner musing counterpart to speech, here chosen from the lexicon's 'meditation' over its 'resounding music'.

In Psa 104:34 the noun 'meditation' with the possessive stands as what the speaker offers and asks to be pleasing to the Lord; it is the musing as an offering, set before the speaker's rejoicing in the Lord.

In Job 15:4 the noun is the reflection before God that the speaker is accused of hindering; in Psa 119:97 and Psa 119:99 it is the law and the testimonies that are the speaker's meditation all day; the sense in all three is sustained reflection, whose object in the Psalm verses is the law.

In Rom 8:6 the noun 'frame of thought, mind-set' appears twice in the same verse, once for the flesh and once for the Spirit, as what is death or life and peace; the lexicon lists 'frame of thought, aspirations' for this verse, and here it is the orientation itself.

In Rom 8:5 the present verb 'to think, set one's mind on' is used of those who live by the flesh or by the Spirit, with the things of each as object; the sense is 'to be minded toward, set the mind on', the directing of the thought.

In 1Ki 18:27 the noun 'musing' is the first of Elijah's mocking alternatives about the god (musing, relieving himself, journey, sleep); it names preoccupation, being occupied in thought, and is a mocking use that departs from the devout musing of the Psalm verses.

In 2Cor 5:16 the perfect verb 'to know' has Christ as object and the phrase 'according to the flesh' as its standard: the sense is to have known and sized up in that way, a settled judgment of him; the ESV renders it regard. The pick-up note on this word is checked against the verse and stands.

In Mat 22:16 and Mar 12:14 the verb 'to look at' is negated and its object is the persons: the sense is 'to look to, have regard for' what a person appears to be, which the lexicon lists for Mt 22:16 and which the ESV renders as caring about opinion; the verse adds 'not swayed by appearances'.
In Pro 18:2 the noun 'heart' is what the fool takes pleasure in laying bare: the ESV renders it his opinion, which is the inner view disclosed; the word is the heart as the holder of what he thinks.

In Act 10:19 the present participle of the verb 'to reflect on' states Peter's continuing reflection on the vision as the Spirit speaks; the sense is sustained pondering of a given object (the vision), the lexicon's 'to ponder, reflect'.

In Luk 2:19 the present participle of the verb 'to throw together' is joined with treasuring up and with the heart: Mary brings the events together in her mind, which is the lexicon's 'to ponder'; the place is stated, in her heart.

In Pro 5:21 the Piel participle with the paths of a man as object means 'to weigh, make level', so the Lord weighs all his paths; the stored sense head 'to envy' for this code disagrees with the lexicon range (weigh, make level) and with the verse, and is flagged as a data error (RG-16), not corrected in the reading.

In Act 17:2, 17:17, 18:4, 18:19 and 24:25 the verb 'to discourse' is used of Paul reasoning with hearers: from the Scriptures in the synagogue (17:2), with Jews and devout persons (17:17), every Sabbath persuading (18:4), with the Jews (18:19), and before Felix on righteousness, self-control and judgment (24:25); the sense is spoken reasoning to persuade.

In 1Cor 13:11 the imperfect verb 'to reckon' is set with speaking and thinking as a childish way of working things out ('I reasoned like a child'); the sense is the process of reckoning something out, with the man's putting it away after.

In Act 19:8 and Act 19:9 the present participle of the verb 'to discourse' states how Paul spoke in the synagogue for three months and then daily in the hall of Tyrannus, with persuading beside it and the kingdom of God as the subject; the sense is spoken reasoning with hearers.

In Luk 9:47 the noun 'reasoning, thought' is what Jesus knows as being in their hearts after the dispute of 9:46; the lexicon lists thought and argument for this word, and here it is the inward line of thought, held in the heart and not spoken.

In Act 10:21, Act 28:20 and 2Ti 1:6 the noun 'cause' is the ground on which something is done or asked: the cause of their coming, and 'for this reason' in Paul's request to see the Jews and in his reminder to Timothy; the sense is the ground or cause.
In Act 28:18 the noun stands in a legal setting, where the Romans found no ground for the death penalty after examining Paul; the lexicon lists the legal sense 'charge, case, ground for accusation'.

In Rom 15:22 the inferential conjunction 'therefore, for this reason' ties Paul's having been hindered from coming to the work he has just described; it is a connective, read for the cause it states (RG-07), and carries no thinking of its own.

In Jam 3:17 the adjective 'compliant, easily persuaded' describes the wisdom from above in a list of its qualities; the lexicon lists this verse, and the sense is readiness to be persuaded, the ESV's 'open to reason'.

In 1Pe 3:15 the noun whose usual sense is 'word' is the thing asked for by the one who asks about the hope: an account, a reason given; the verse sets it with being prepared to make a defense, so here the word is an explanation and departs from the sense of a spoken word.

In Jos 5:4 and 1Ki 11:27 the noun 'word, matter' stands in 'this is the reason why': it is the matter that accounts for what follows, an explanation of a cause; the usual senses speech and thing are not the sense here.

In Eze 19:10 the stored word is the Qal perfect, third feminine singular, of the verb 'to be', the copula of 'your mother was like a vine'; it is not a word of reasoning and does not render 'by reason of' (which belongs to the preposition and the noun in the clause). The alignment into the unit 'reason' is flagged as a data error (RG-16), not corrected in the reading.

In Job 1:9 and Pro 3:30 the adverb 'for nothing, without cause' stands in the question and the prohibition: Job fears God, and a man is not to be contended with, for no cause; the sense is the absence of ground, which the ESV gives as 'for no reason'.

In Isa 1:18 the verb whose usual sense is 'to rebuke, prove' stands in the Niphal cohortative, 'let us reason together': an invitation to argue the case out between the Lord and the people, followed by what the Lord says; the sense is to set a case before one another, not to rebuke.

In 1Sa 20:29 the adverb 'so, therefore' in the phrase the ESV gives as 'for this reason' ties Jonathan's report that David has not come to the family sacrifice and to his brother's command; it is a connective of consequence.

In Gen 41:31 and Gen 47:13 the noun 'face' is joined with a preposition and the famine in the phrase the ESV renders 'by reason of the famine': it states the cause of the plenty being unknown and of the lands languishing; it is a prepositional use, not the face.

In Luk 22:24 the verb 'to think' stands in a clause about which of the disciples is to be regarded as greatest: it is the standing assigned to a person, 'to be reckoned', and not what the subject thinks.

In Rom 2:26 and Rom 8:36 the verb 'to reckon' is passive and carries an 'as': the uncircumcised will be counted as circumcision, and the believers are counted as sheep for slaughter; the sense is 'to be counted as', a status assigned.

In Gen 31:15, Psa 44:22, Lam 4:2 and Hos 8:12 the Niphal perfect of the verb 'to reckon' is followed by 'as' and the thing compared: foreigners, sheep to be slaughtered, earthen pots, a strange thing; the sense is 'to be accounted as', the status others give.

In Isa 29:16 and Isa 29:17 the Niphal imperfect of the verb 'to reckon' is in two questions with 'as' and the thing compared (the potter as clay; the fruitful field as a forest); the sense is 'to be counted as', a status turned upside down.

In 2Cor 5:16 the present verb 'to know' with 'thus' no longer is the second half of the verse's contrast with the earlier regarding of Christ; the sense is to know or size up, now ended as a way of knowing him.

In 2Th 3:15 and 1Ti 6:1 the present imperative of the verb 'to lead, count' has an 'as' complement: do not count him as an enemy, let bondservants count their masters as worthy of honor; the sense is 'to esteem as', a judgment of status.

In 1Cor 4:1 and 1Pe 5:12 the verb 'to reckon' has a person as object and an 'as' complement: in 1Cor 4:1 how the apostles are to be taken, as servants and stewards, and in 1Pe 5:12 Peter's estimate of Silvanus as a faithful brother; the sense is 'to consider as'.

In Col 2:16 the noun 'part, share' stands in a prepositional idiom ('in a part of') that introduces the topics of food, drink, festival, new moon and Sabbath; it means 'with regard to' and is not a thinking word, which departs from the dictionary sense 'part'.

In 2Cor 5:16 the perfect verb 'to know' has 'no one' as object and 'according to the flesh' as its standard; the lexicon lists 'to have regard for one, to pay attention to' for the code, and the verse sets it before the later regard for Christ.

In Exo 5:9 the negative 'not' (used with a verb: let not) stands in the jussive and bears on the regarding of lying words (H8159 in the same verse): the work is to be heavier so that the men do not pay heed; the verse states its reach.

In Psa 28:5 the Qal imperfect of the verb 'to discern' is negated and has the works of the Lord as object: they do not discern or give heed to them; the sense is attentive understanding, which the verse says is lacking in the wicked.

In Ecc 3:18 the noun 'cause, manner' stands in an idiom that opens 'I said in my heart': it means 'with regard to' the children of man and is a prepositional use, not a word of thought; it departs from the dictionary sense 'cause'.

In Isa 13:17 and Isa 33:8 the Qal of the verb 'to reckon' is negated and has silver and man as objects: the Medes have no regard for silver, there is no regard for man; the sense is 'to esteem, value', the lexicon's 'to esteem, value, regard'.

In Job 9:21, Psa 144:3 and Pro 12:10 the verb 'to know' means to take knowing account of someone with care: the speaker does not regard himself, the Lord regards man, and the righteous regards the life of his beast; the sense is 'to take note of, acknowledge'.
In Job 9:21 the negative 'not' follows 'I regard' (H3045 in the same verse) and bears on it: the verse states that he does not regard himself; the reach is the verb of regarding.

In 1Sa 25:25 the noun 'heart' is not the speaker's word for a faculty but the object-word of an idiom of setting the heart on someone, in the plea that the lord not take Nabal to heart; the ESV renders it 'regard', and the unit is shared with the verb.

In Psa 74:20, Isa 5:12 and Lam 4:16 the Hiphil of the verb 'to look' means to look upon with regard: in Psa 74:20 the covenant is the object the Lord is asked to look to, in Isa 5:12 the feasters give no heed to what the Lord has done, in Lam 4:16 the Lord's looking on them is withdrawn; it includes both attention and favour.

In Jer 24:5 the Hiphil of the verb 'to recognize' has the exiles as object and 'as good' as complement: the Lord will recognise and regard them as good; the sense is 'to acknowledge, regard', as the lexicon lists the Hiphil.

In 2Ki 3:14 the verb 'to lift' is part of the idiom 'to lift the face of someone', the sense given by the lexicon head 'favour, honour': Elisha says he has regard for Jehoshaphat, which is why he acts; it is respect shown, not lifting.

In 1Sa 1:16 the verb 'to give, put' stands in a plea not to be set as a worthless woman: the speaker asks not to be reckoned as one; the verb of giving is used of reckoning, which departs from its first sense.

In Lev 19:23 the verb 'to count uncircumcised' is a denominative of the foreskin: the fruit of a newly planted tree is to be counted as uncircumcised, which the verse spells out as forbidden for three years; the sense is 'to treat as foreskin, withheld'.

In Deu 9:27 and 2Ch 6:19 the verb 'to turn' is used with a prepositional object of what the Lord is asked to turn toward or not to turn toward: do not regard the stubbornness, have regard to the prayer; it is attention directed, not a physical turning.

In Psa 80:14 the Qal imperative 'visit' follows 'look down from heaven, and see' and has the vine as object: the sense is to attend to and care for, which the lexicon lists for the code (to attend to, look after, care for).

In Deu 33:9 and Job 37:24 the verb 'to see' is negated: in Deu 33:9 the Levite's words of his parents, in Job 37:24 God's attitude to the self-wise; the sense is to look upon with regard, which the lexicon lists, here withheld.
In Job 35:13 the verb 'to behold' is negated and has the empty cry as object: the Almighty does not look upon it; the sense is to take notice of, the lexicon's 'to regard'.

In Job 34:27 the Hiphil perfect of the verb 'to be prudent' is negated and has all his ways as object: they had no regard for them; the sense is 'to give heed to, consider', which the lexicon lists for the Hiphil.

In 2Ch 5:11 the verb 'to keep, observe' is in a phrase about the priests being present without regard to their divisions; the sense is not keeping to the order of their courses, observing a rule, which the ESV gives as 'regard'.

In Gen 4:5, Exo 5:9 and Psa 119:117 the verb 'to gaze at' is used of regard, with its object a person's offering, lying words and the Lord's statutes: Cain's offering was not looked on, the men are not to look to lying words, the psalmist asks to look continually at the statutes.

In Mar 8:33 the present verb 'to think, set the mind on' is negated for Peter and set against its opposite object in the rebuke of Jesus, so that what the mind is directed to is the contrast; the sense is the directing of the thinking, as in Rom 8:5.

In Rom 2:3 the connective 'but, and' opens the question with the verb of reckoning (G3049 in the same verse), so that the sentence runs on from the accusation of 2:1; it is read as a connective, not as a word of supposing.

In Jam 4:5 the present verb 'to think' stands in a question put to the readers: do you suppose that the Scripture speaks to no purpose; the sense is 'to suppose, imagine', set in a rhetorical question.

In Joh 21:25 and Jam 1:7 the present verb 'to suppose' is set in the first person (the writer's estimate that the world could not contain the books) and in a third-person prohibition (that person must not suppose he will receive); the sense is 'to suppose, expect'.

In Luk 7:43 and Act 2:15 the verb 'to take up, suppose' is used of a considered view: Simon's answer 'I suppose' and the charge of drunkenness 'as you suppose'; the sense is 'to take it that', an assumption offered.
In Act 13:25 the present verb 'to suppose, suspect' is in Paul's quotation of John: what do you suppose that I am; the sense is 'to suspect, take to be'.

In Gen 18:28-32 the adverb 'perhaps' is the word with which Abraham sets a conceivable number of righteous to the Lord, five times with the number falling from forty-five to ten; it introduces a case put for argument, which the ESV renders 'suppose'.

In 2Sa 13:32 and 2Sa 13:33 the verb 'to say' stands in 'let not my lord suppose' that all the king's sons are dead: the lexicon lists 'to say in one's heart, to think' for the Qal, and the verse gives the content of what he is not to think.

In Luk 2:44, Act 14:19 and Act 16:27 the participle of the verb 'to think' states an assumption on which a step is taken: they went a day's journey, they dragged Paul out, the jailer drew his sword; the sense is 'supposing', an assumption of a state of affairs.

In Phili 1:17 the present participle 'to suppose' states the intention of those who proclaim Christ out of selfish ambition: they suppose or intend to afflict Paul in his imprisonment; the sense is 'to suppose, expect'.

In Luk 11:17 the noun 'thought' is what Jesus knows before he answers; the lexicon lists the word for this verse alone, and the sense is an inward thought known to him.

In Luk 1:51 the noun 'mind, thinking' is in the dative with the hearts: the proud are scattered in the thinking of their hearts; the lexicon gives the part of the inner person that thinks, whose seat is the heart.

In Psa 139:2 the noun 'thought, purpose' (singular, with the speaker's suffix) is what the Lord discerns from afar, beside his sitting and rising; the sense is the speaker's inner thought, known to God.
In Psa 139:17 the plural noun 'thoughts' is God's own, called precious and too vast to be counted; the sense is the thinking of God, set against the speaker's thought of 139:2.

In Dan 2:29 and Dan 2:30 the Aramaic noun 'thought' is what came to the king on his bed concerning what would be, and the thoughts of his mind that Daniel is to make known; the sense is thoughts of the mind, shown to Daniel by revelation.

In Luk 12:17 the imperfect verb 'to reason through' is followed by 'to himself' and the question of what to do with the crops: the man deliberates inwardly; the lexicon lists 'to reason, deliberate, ponder', and the unit also holds the verb 'to say' (G3004G).

In Mar 6:49, Luk 24:37, Joh 11:13, Joh 13:29 and Act 12:9 the verb 'to think' states a supposition formed from what is seen or heard: a ghost, a spirit, rest in sleep, a purchase, a vision; in each the verse shows it to be a mistaken or partial supposition.
In 2Cor 9:5 and Phili 2:25 the verb 'to lead, count' states a considered judgment that something is necessary: urging the brothers to go ahead, sending Epaphroditus; the sense is 'to judge, deem'.

In Act 26:8 the passive verb 'to judge' has 'incredible' as complement: the question is whether it is judged incredible that God raises the dead; the sense is 'to be judged, reckoned to be', an estimate held by the hearers.

In Luk 12:17 the participle of the verb 'to say' is the second word of the unit 'thought' (the verb G1260 beside it): the man speaks within himself, so the saying is inner speech, which departs from the verb's usual sense of spoken words.

In 1Ti 3:7 the noun 'testimony, reputation' is the thing the overseer must have from outsiders; the lexicon lists the reputation sense, and the ESV renders it as being well thought of: it is the estimate outsiders hold of him.
In 2Cor 10:5 the noun 'thought' is the object of the taking captive to obey Christ, set beside arguments and lofty opinions; the sense is the product of the mind, every one of them.

In Mat 20:10 and Act 8:20 the verb 'to think, suppose' states an expectation or assumption on which the person acts: the first hired expected more, Simon assumed he could buy the gift; the sense is 'to suppose, expect'.
In 1Cor 13:11 the imperfect verb 'to be minded' stands between speaking and reasoning as a way of working things out in childhood; the sense is a mode of thinking, the mind-set of a child.

In Jon 1:6 the adverb 'perhaps' opens the captain's hope that the god will take notice of them (the verb of giving thought, H6245B, is in the same verse); it marks a possibility, not a thought of its own.

In Gen 20:11, 26:9, 32:20, Exo 2:14, Jos 22:28, Jdg 3:24, 1Sa 16:6, 18:11, 18:17, 18:21, 20:26, 2Sa 14:15, 14:17, 2Ki 5:11, 20:19, Job 29:18, Psa 94:18, Isa 39:8, Jer 3:7 and Eze 20:32 the verb 'to say' introduces what a person says to himself and the verse gives the thought as quoted speech; the sense is 'to say in one's heart, to think'.

In Gen 31:31, Jdg 15:2 and Jer 3:19 the verb 'to say' introduces an assumption or expectation in an indirect clause: that Laban would take his daughters, that she utterly hated her, that you would call me Father; the sense is 'to think, assume' with the thought stated as what he took to be so.

In Rut 4:4 and 2Sa 21:16 the verb 'to say' states a purpose: to tell the kinsman of the matter, and to kill David; it is an intention held, which departs from the sense of a belief or assumption in the other verses.

In Pro 14:15 and Pro 21:29 the Qal imperfect of the verb 'to discern' has the steps and the ways as object and sets the prudent and the upright against the simple and the wicked; the sense is 'to give careful thought to, attend to', which the lexicon lists as 'to give heed to'.

In Deu 15:9 the noun 'word, matter' is the thing that might be present in the heart, an unworthy matter that leads to the grudging look and giving nothing; the noun for a word is used of what is held inwardly, which departs from its sense of speech.
In Num 33:56 the Piel perfect of the verb 'to liken, imagine' states what the Lord purposed to do to the Canaanites and will now do to Israel; the sense is 'to purpose, devise', a plan held.
In Psa 48:9 the Piel perfect of the verb 'to imagine, think' has the steadfast love as object and the temple as place: the worshippers have reflected on it; the sense is 'to ponder, think on'.

In Psa 50:21 the Piel perfect of the verb 'to imagine' states the false supposition of the wicked about God, answered by the Lord's rebuke; the sense is 'to suppose, imagine', which the lexicon lists for the Piel.

In Deu 15:9 the verb 'to be' (jussive) is the 'lest there be' of the clause, joined in the unit 'thought' with the noun for the matter (H1697G, same verse); it is the existential copula and not a word of thought.
In Lam 1:9 the Qal perfect of the verb 'to remember' is negated: she did not call her future to mind, which the verse sets before her fall; the sense is 'to remember, take thought of', withheld.
In 1Sa 18:25 the Qal perfect of the verb 'to plan' states Saul's purpose in the bride-price he sets: to bring about David's fall; the sense is 'to devise, plan' with a harmful end.
In Psa 40:17 the Qal imperfect of the verb 'to plan' has the Lord as subject and the poor and needy speaker as the one he thinks on; the sense is 'to take thought for', the planning of care.

In Gen 38:15 the wayyiqtol of the verb 'to reckon' states the conclusion Judah drew from her covered face: he took her for a prostitute; the sense is 'to take to be', a judgment formed from appearance.

In Psa 73:16 the Piel wayyiqtol of the verb 'to reckon' states the speaker's attempt to work out the prosperity of the wicked, which he found wearisome; the sense is 'to set the mind to understand', an effortful working out.

In Ecc 9:10 the noun 'account, reasoning' is in a list with work, knowledge and wisdom that are not in Sheol; the lexicon gives 'account, reasoning, reckoning', and the sense is the activity of reckoning.
In 1Ch 28:9 the noun 'thought, device' is paired with plan as what the Lord understands when he searches all hearts; the sense is the thought or device of a heart, known to him.

In 2Sa 3:19 the noun 'eye' is in the idiom 'in the eyes of' with Israel and Benjamin: what seemed good in their view; the ESV renders it 'thought good', and the eye is the standpoint of the judgment, not the organ of sight.

In Jon 1:6 the Hithpael verb 'to think' states the hope that the god will take thought of the sailors so that they do not perish; the sense is 'to give thought, take notice', and the verse sets it after perhaps (H0194).

In Job 12:5 the noun 'thought' in the construct stands for the attitude of the one at ease toward misfortune: contempt for it; the lexicon gives 'thought, idea', and the sense is the opinion of the comfortable.

In Mic 2:8 the Qal participle of the verb 'to return' in the construct with war is the description of the trusting passersby: those who come back from war; the ESV gives it as 'no thought of war', but the stored word is the returning, not a word of thought.
In Amo 4:13 the noun 'thought, musing' with the suffix is what the Lord declares to man; the sense is a person's own thought, laid open by the one who made the mountains.

In Ecc 12:9 the Piel perfect of the verb 'to weigh' is the first of three acts of the Preacher in handling proverbs (weighing, studying, arranging); the lexicon lists 'weigh, test, consider', and here it is a careful judging of each proverb before it is set in order.

In 1Cor 14:29 the present imperative of the verb 'to distinguish, judge' is given to the others when two or three prophets have spoken: they are to evaluate what is said; the sense is 'to discern, judge' between the sayings.

In Zep 1:11 the adjective 'laden' (plural construct) describes the traders as those loaded with silver; the ESV renders it as weighing out silver, but the stored word is the adjective of being laden, not a verb of weighing.

In Ezr 8:29 the Qal imperfect of the verb 'to weigh' is the act of weighing the silver and the vessels before the priests, Levites and heads of fathers' houses; the sense is 'to weigh out' for an accounting, a physical weighing and not a mental one.

The surfaces of this group share one kind of meaning: to hold something to be so. The codes carry it as thinking and supposing (G1380, G3543, G3633, G5274, G5282), as saying within oneself (H0559, whose Qal sense includes 'to say in one's heart, to think'), as reckoning and imagining (H2803J, H1819) and as the case put forward with perhaps (H0194). The verses state what is held, often as a quoted thought: Mat 17:25, Joh 11:13, Gen 20:11, 1Sa 20:3, Job 35:2, Gen 18:28.

The surfaces of this group share one kind of meaning: giving attention to a matter and going over it. The codes carry it as musing and meditating (H7878, H1897, H7881, H1900), as considering and setting the heart on a thing (H2803H, H7760K, H3820A, H7896K), as reflecting and observing (G1760, G2657), as giving heed with insight (H7919A) and as weighing up (H0239, G1252, H6424); the lexicon also lists plain weights and weighing out (H4948, H8254, H5187). The verses name what is attended to: Psa 119:15, Jos 1:8, Act 10:19, Luk 2:19, Ecc 12:9, 1Cor 14:29.

The surfaces of this group share one kind of meaning: giving a ground, and arguing a case by grounds. The codes carry it as reasoning and discussing (G1256, G1261, H3198 in the sense of arguing a case), and as the ground or cause itself (G0156 cause and charge, G1352 therefore, G1223 and G5484 because of, H1697M a matter that accounts for, H3651C therefore, H2600 without cause). The verses show the exchange of grounds or the ground stated: Act 17:2, Act 24:25, Act 10:21, Rom 15:22, Isa 1:18, Job 1:9.

The surfaces of this group share one meaning: the set or direction of the mind. The two codes carry it as the verb 'to think, set the mind on' (G5426) and the noun 'frame of thought, aspiration' (G5427, which the lexicon lists for Rom 8:6, 8:7 and 8:27). The verses give what the mind is set on, against an opposite: Rom 8:5, Rom 8:6, Mar 8:33.

The surfaces of this group share one kind of meaning: taking account of someone or something, and the standing given it. The codes carry it as looking on and heeding (H8159, H5027, H7200G, H7789, H6485I), as knowing in the sense of acknowledging (H3045, H5234A, G1097, G6063), as lifting the face in favour (H5375Q) and as counting or esteeming as (H2803H, H2803J, G3049, G2233). The verses give the object regarded or the status it is counted as: Gen 4:5, Psa 74:20, Pro 12:10, Rom 2:26, Psa 44:22, 2Cor 5:16.

The surfaces of this group share one kind of meaning: a thought, view or device, as the thing a person holds or brings forth. The codes carry it as thought and device (H4284, H4209, H7454, H7476, H4093, H5587B, G1761, G3540), as reasoning (G1261, G3053), as mind and the thing it holds (G1271, G1270) and as opinion and knowledge declared (H1843, H4906). The verses speak of it as present in a person, known to another or set against another: Gen 6:5, Isa 55:8, Luk 5:22, Dan 4:19, Job 32:10, Psa 139:2.

The surfaces of this group share one kind of meaning: forming or bringing forth within. The codes carry it as conceiving (H2029, whose Poel sense is 'to conceive, contrive, devise'; H3179; G4815), as being with child (H2030A) and as planning and devising (H2803I); the verses give both a child conceived (Jdg 13:7, Mat 1:23, Psa 51:5) and trouble or harm conceived or devised (Job 15:35, Psa 41:7).

The lexicon entries bear the grouping out: the codes with the largest counts are the verbs of thinking and supposing (G1380 to think, G3543 to think, G3633 and G5282 to suppose, G5274 to take up, suppose) and the verb to say, whose Qal sense in the lexicon includes saying in one's heart and so thinking (H0559, the largest code with 40 occurrences), with H2803J (think, imagine), H1819 (to imagine, think), H2803I (to plan, devise), H5452 (to think, intend) and H6245B (to think). H0194 'perhaps, suppose' gives the case put forward. Codes that link the group to its usage: H0559 for the thought quoted to oneself and G1380 and G3543 for the supposition acted on. The group definition is a supposition or estimate held. Codes in these units that do not carry the meaning themselves, because the unit aligns a neighbouring word into it, are the connectives and function words (G1161, G2532, H3588A, H0834A, H0413, H0853, H1931, H2009, H1961); the lexicon gives them their own senses (then, and, for, which, to, the object marker, he, behold, to be), and stage 1 read them in their verses.

The lexicon entries bear the grouping out for most of the group: the verbs of musing and meditating (H7878 to muse, 11 occurrences; H1897 to mutter, meditate; H7742 to meditate; the nouns H7881, H1902H and H1900 meditation), of considering and reflecting (H2803H to count, regard; H7760K and H7896K to set, consider; H7200H to examine, consider; G1760 to reflect on; G2657 to observe; H7920 to contemplate; H7919A to give heed) and of pondering and weighing up (G4820 to ponder, confer; H0239 to ponder, weigh; H6424 to weigh, make level; G1252 to judge). Codes that link the group to its usage are H7878 and H1897 for the musing on a named object and H7760K with H3820A (heart) for the idiom of setting the heart. The lexicon also lists physical senses among the codes: H4948 weight (4 occurrences), H8254 to weigh out, H5187 laden; and the stored sense head of H6424 reads 'to envy' against a range of weigh, make level. The group definition is giving attention to a matter and going over it, with the weights outside that meaning.

The lexicon entries bear the grouping out only partly: the reasoning codes are G1256 (to reason, discuss, argue, 7 occurrences), G1261 (reasoning), G3049 (to reckon) and H3198 (to prove, argue a case), and the ground or cause codes are G0156 (cause, charge), G1352 (therefore, for this reason), G1223 and G5484 (because of), G5124, H6440I and H1697M (because), H3651C (so, therefore) and H2600 (without cause). The codes that link the group to its usage are G1256 for the spoken reasoning in the synagogue and G0156 for the cause given. Several codes are small words aligned into the units: G2596 (according to), G0302 (if), G1519 (toward), H5921A (upon), G5124 (that), H1961 (to be); and G2138 (compliant), G3056 (word) and H4486 (knowledge) have senses of their own that the verses use for reasonableness, an account and knowledge. The group definition is giving a ground and arguing a case by grounds; the causal codes are the larger share by occurrence.

The lexicon entries bear the grouping out fully: G5426 is 'to think, set the mind on, hold an attitude' and G5427 is the noun 'frame of thought, purpose, aspiration', which the lexicon lists for Rom 8:6, 8:7 and 8:27. The two codes are the verb and its noun and carry the same meaning, the set of the mind; they link the group to its usage in Rom 8:5, Rom 8:6 and Mar 8:33. The group definition is the set or direction of the mind.

The lexicon entries bear the grouping out for most of the group: the codes of looking on and heeding (H8159 to gaze, H5027 to look, H7200G to see, H7789 to see, H6485I to visit, attend to), of knowing in the sense of acknowledging (H3045 to know, H5234A to recognise, G1097 and G6063 to know), of favour (H5375Q to lift, favour) and of counting and esteeming as (H2803H to count, regard as, 6 occurrences; H2803J; G3049 to count; G2233 to lead, count). The codes that link the group to its usage are H2803H and G3049 for the status a thing is counted as and H8159, H5027 and H3045 for the regard paid. Several codes are small words aligned into the units: H0408 and H3808 (not, negators), H9006 (from), H0853 (object marker), G4012 (about), G3313 (part, in the idiom 'in regard to'), H1700 (cause, 'with regard to') and H3820A (heart, in an idiom). The group definition is taking account of someone or something and the standing given it.

The lexicon entries bear the grouping out: the codes are the nouns for what the mind holds or brings forth, thought and device (H4284, 19 occurrences; H4209; H7454; H7476; H4093; H5587B disquietings; G1761 reflection; G3540 mind, thought; G1270 thought), reasoning and mind (G1261; G3053 thought; G1271 mind), and opinion and knowledge declared (H1843; H4906 figure, conceit). The codes that link the group to its usage are H4284 and G1261, which together are 26 of the occurrences. Codes whose own sense differs from the group are G0991 (to see, here a looking at persons), H3820A (heart, in an idiom), H1697I (matter), H1902H (meditation), G3588 (the, with no morph stored) and H8312 (anxiety), which the units align into the surface. The group definition is a thought, view or device as the thing a person holds or brings forth.

The lexicon entries bear the grouping out only for part of the group: the codes of conceiving and being with child are H2029 (to conceive; the Poel sense is to contrive, devise; 5 occurrences), H3179 (to conceive), H2030A (pregnant), G4815 (to seize, conceive, help) and H2232 (to sow, the Niphal to be made pregnant), and the code of planning is H2803I (to plan, devise). G2192 (to have), G2602 (beginning, foundation, conception in Heb 11:11), G4690G (seed) and G1722 (in) are the codes of the Greek idioms rendered as conceive. The codes that link the group to its usage are H2029 and H2030A for the bearing of a child and of trouble. The group definition is forming or bringing forth within; the lexicon gives the bodily sense of conceiving a child more weight than the sense of devising.

Anger stands with the group in Gen 18:30, Gen 18:32 and 2Ki 5:11. In all three the anger is named before the supposition in the verse: the Lord's anger that Abraham asks not to be roused, and Naaman's anger, which is 4 words before the thought of 2Ki 5:11; the stored positions are not given for the two Genesis verses.

Believing stands with the group in Pro 14:15, Rom 12:3, Phili 3:4 and Jam 1:26. In Pro 14:15 'believes' is 3 words before the member and is set against giving thought; in the other three the thing thought concerns oneself and its partner is faith (6 after, Rom 12:3), confidence (6 before and 1 after, Phili 3:4) and religion (12 after, Jam 1:26).

Blessing words stand with the group at a distance in Rom 12:3, 2Cor 9:5 and Heb 10:29: grace 11 words before the member in Rom 12:3 and 16 after it in Heb 10:29, and a willing gift 16 after in 2Cor 9:5. The distances show the partner is in another clause of the verse, not in the clause of the member.

Calling stands with the group in Gen 26:9, 2Ki 5:11, Jer 3:19 and Jon 1:6. In 2Ki 5:11 (4 after) and Jer 3:19 (1 after) the call is part of what was expected; in Jon 1:6 it is the command to call on his god, 4 words before the hope that the god will give a thought; in Gen 26:9 the call (Abimelech calling Isaac) is 12 words before and a separate act.

War words stand with the group in 1Sa 18:17, 2Ki 18:20, Isa 36:5 and Mic 2:8. In 2Ki 18:20 and Isa 36:5 'war' is 5 words after the member and is what the supposed strategy and power are for; in 1Sa 18:17 'fight' is 4 and 'battles' 2 words before the member and belong to Saul's plan; in Mic 2:8 'war' is 1 word after.

Comfort stands with the group in Job 12:5, Psa 119:52 and Joh 11:31. In Psa 119:52 the thinking and the comfort are in one clause, comfort 4 words after; in Job 12:5 'ease' is 1 word after the thought of the at-ease; in Joh 11:31 the consoling stands 10 words before the supposition that explains why they followed her.

Commanding stands with the group in Num 36:6, 2Sa 13:32, Psa 50:21, Rom 12:3 and 1Cor 14:37. In Num 36:6 the Lord's commands are 4 words before the member; in Psa 50:21 'charge' is 2 words after 'you thought'; in 1Cor 14:37 the command (11 words after) is what the one who thinks he is a prophet is to acknowledge; in 2Sa 13:32 (12 after) and Rom 12:3 (8 after) the partner is in a later clause.

Concealing stands with the group in Gen 38:15, 2Ki 7:12 and Psa 64:5. In Gen 38:15 the covering is 2 words after the member and is the ground of Judah's supposition; in 2Ki 7:12 'hide' is 2 words and in Psa 64:5 'secretly' 1 word before the thought, so the thought is quoted beside hiding.

Judging stands with the group in Exo 2:14, Luk 7:43, Joh 5:45 and Rom 2:3. In Joh 5:45 (accuse, 3 after) and Rom 2:3 (judge, 3 after) the thing supposed concerns accusation or judgment; in Luk 7:43 the judging (8 after) is the answer given to the supposition; in Exo 2:14 'judge' is 8 words before, in the question the accuser puts.

Persuading stands with the group in Act 14:19, Rom 14:14 and 2Cor 10:5. In Act 14:19 (8 before) and Rom 14:14 (13 before) the persuading is before the member; in 2Cor 10:5 the partner is obeying, 3 words after: the thought is taken captive so as to obey.

Deceiving stands with the group in 1Cor 3:18, Gal 6:3 and Jam 1:26: 6 words before the member in 1Cor 3:18, 5 after in Gal 6:3 and 8 after in Jam 1:26. In all three the person thinks something of himself (wise, something, religious) and the verse names self-deception beside it.

Departing stands with the group in 1Sa 27:11, Ecc 9:10, Mat 18:12 and Joh 11:31: leave 5 words before in 1Sa 27:11, going 7 after in Ecc 9:10, leave 12 after in Mat 18:12 and going 2 after in Joh 11:31. Only in Joh 11:31 is the departure the act that the supposition explains (they followed her out, supposing she went to weep).

Desire words stand with the group in 1Sa 18:25, 1Ch 28:9 and Jam 4:5: 'desires' 12 words before in 1Sa 18:25, 'willing' 9 before in 1Ch 28:9, 'yearns' 5 after in Jam 4:5. The surface 'will' of 2Sa 14:17 (4 after) and 2Ki 7:12 (13 before) is the particle and verb of the quoted speech, not a desire.

Destroying stands with the group in Gen 18:28, 18:31, 18:32, Isa 10:7 and 2Cor 10:5. In Gen 18 the destroying is what the Lord is asked not to do under each supposed number (positions not stored); in Isa 10:7 it is 3 words after the member and is in the heart of the one who plans; in 2Cor 10:5 it is 12 words before and is an act upon arguments.

Death words stand with the group in seven verses. In Gen 26:9, Job 29:18 and Jon 1:6 the dying or perishing is 2 words after the member and is the content of the thought; in Joh 11:13 death is 3 words before and the disciples suppose something else; in Act 8:20 perishing is 4 before, in 1Cor 4:9 death is 7 after and in 1Sa 20:3 15 after.

Enduring stands with the group in 2Ch 13:8, Jer 40:5, 1Cor 4:9 and 1Cor 7:26. In 2Ch 13:8 'withstand' is 1 word after the thought to withstand; in 1Cor 7:26 'remain' is 9 after and is what is judged good; in 1Cor 4:9 'last' is 6 after; in Jer 40:5 'remain' is 20 words before.

Escaping stands with the group in Gen 32:8, Est 4:13, Act 16:27 and Rom 2:3: 9 words after in Gen 32:8, 4 after in Est 4:13, 2 after in Act 16:27, 10 after in Rom 2:3. In every verse the escape is part of what is supposed: hoped for, denied, assumed by the jailer, or put as a question.

Evil stands with the group in 2Sa 14:17, Psa 64:5, Pro 21:29, Mat 9:4, 1Cor 14:20 and 1Ti 6:5. In Mat 9:4 'evil' is 1 word after the member and is what is thought; in Psa 64:5 it is 5 words before and in 1Ti 6:5 'depraved' 5 before; in Pro 21:29 the wicked is 5 before and set against the upright who gives thought; in 1Cor 14:20 evil is 2 before and is set against mature thinking.

Fear stands with the group in six verses. In Gen 31:31, Exo 2:14, 2Sa 14:15 and Neh 6:9 the fear is 1 to 2 words before the thought and the thought comes from it; in Luk 24:37 the startled and frightened are 3 and 1 words before; in Gen 20:11 the fear is of God and is 3 words after, as what the thought says is absent.

Folly stands with the group in Pro 14:15, Rom 1:21, 1Cor 3:18, 2Cor 11:16 and 2Cor 12:6: 'simple' 4 words before in Pro 14:15, 'foolish' 2 after in Rom 1:21, 'fool' 7 after in 1Cor 3:18, 'foolish' 2 and 'fool' 9 after in 2Cor 11:16, 'fool' 8 before in 2Cor 12:6. Folly is what a person is judged to be or becomes in the thinking.

Security stands with the group in 2Ki 20:19, 2Ch 32:1, Isa 39:8 and Jer 40:5. In 2Ki 20:19 (4 after) and Isa 39:8 (3 after) security is the content of Hezekiah's thought; in 2Ch 32:1 the fortified cities are 2 words before and are what is planned against; in Jer 40:5 'guard' is 4 after.

The partner is the surface 'surely' (codes H0403, H2009, H0389, H3588A, H1931, H3318G, H0413) in five Hebrew verses, where it stands inside the quoted thought (1 to 5 words after the member in 1Sa 20:26 and 2Ki 5:11; positions not stored in the others), and hearing proper in Mat 6:7 (heard, 2 after), Luk 8:18 (hear, 12 before) and 2Cor 12:6 (hears, 7 after).

Heart or mind stands with the group in all ten verses. It is within three words of the member in Deu 15:9 and 2Sa 13:33 (1), Isa 10:7 (2), Eze 20:32 and Rom 1:21 (3); at 4 in 1Ch 28:9 (hearts), Mat 9:4 and 1Ti 6:5; at 6 in Eze 11:5; and at 10 in Jam 1:26 and 1Ch 28:9 (heart). The verses name the heart or mind as the place of the thought.

Honor stands with the group in 2Sa 10:3, 1Ch 19:3, Act 13:25, Rom 1:21, 1Cor 12:23 and 1Ti 3:7. In 2Sa 10:3 and 1Ch 19:3 'honoring' is 4 words after the member in the question whether David honors; in 1Cor 12:23 'less honorable' is 1 and 'honor' 3 after; in 1Ti 3:7 the opposite, disgrace, is 6 after.

Intending stands with the group in 1Ch 28:9, Psa 64:5, Isa 10:7, Joh 11:13, Act 27:13 and Jam 4:5. The partner words are of the same kind as the member in 1Ch 28:9 (plan, 1 before), Psa 64:5 (purpose, 4 before) and Isa 10:7 (intend, 4 before); in Joh 11:13 'meant' is 2 after and is what Jesus meant, which they supposed otherwise; in Act 27:13 and Jam 4:5 'purpose' is 2 and 1 after.

Killing stands with the group in Exo 2:14, 2Sa 13:32, 2Sa 21:16, Luk 13:4, Joh 16:2 and Act 16:27. In 2Sa 13:32 and 2Sa 21:16 the killing is 1 word after the member and is what is supposed or intended; in Luk 13:4, Joh 16:2 and Act 16:27 it is 2 words before, and in Joh 16:2 the killer supposes he serves God.

Knowing stands with the group in thirteen verses. In 1Cor 8:2 (knows 1 after, know 5 after) and Ecc 9:10 (knowledge 1 after) knowledge is beside the member; in Mat 9:4 and Eze 11:5 what is known is another's thought (Jesus knowing their thoughts, the Lord knowing what comes into the mind); in 1Sa 20:3 the knowing (6 before, 3 after) is the father's knowledge of David's favour and Jonathan's not knowing; elsewhere it is 3 to 15 words away (Exo 2:14, Rut 4:4, 2Ki 7:12, 1Ch 28:9, Act 12:9, Rom 1:21, Rom 14:14, 2Cor 10:5).

Work stands with the group in Neh 6:9, Ecc 9:10, Mat 21:28 and Eph 3:20: 4 words after in Neh 6:9, 1 before in Ecc 9:10 (where work and thought are two things not in Sheol), 11 after in Mat 21:28 and 3 after in Eph 3:20 (the power at work set beside what we think).

Crying and weeping stand with the group in Deu 15:9 (cry, 14 after, the cry to the Lord), Mar 6:49 (cried out, 4 after), Joh 11:31 (weep, 6 after) and Joh 20:15 (weeping, position not stored). In the three Gospel verses the crying or weeping follows or accompanies a supposition: a ghost, a visit to the tomb, a gardener.

Life and death words stand with the group in eight verses. 'Dead' is the partner in 2Sa 13:32 (9 after), 2Sa 13:33 (4 after), Act 14:19 (2 after) and Act 26:8 (7 after); in the first three the supposition is that someone is dead; 'alive' or 'lives' is the partner in 1Sa 20:3 (9), 2Ki 7:12 (5) and 1Sa 27:11 and Luk 13:4 (11 and 8 after).

Loyalty stands with the group in 2Ch 32:1, Psa 48:9 and Psa 94:18. In both Psalm verses steadfast love is within 3 words after the member: in Psa 48:9 (1 after) it is what is thought on, in Psa 94:18 (3 after) it is what held the speaker up after he thought his foot slips; in 2Ch 32:1 faithfulness is 10 words before.

Silence and rest stand with the group in 2Sa 14:17 (rest, 5 after), Psa 50:21 (silent, 1 before), 1Cor 7:40 (remains, 3 before) and 1Pe 4:1 (ceased, 5 after). Only in Psa 50:21 is the silence the ground of the supposition (the speaker has been silent and is supposed to be like the other).

A gift stands with the group in Gen 32:20 (present, 3 after, the means of appeasing) and Jer 40:5 (present, 7 after). In Rut 4:4 the partner word is 'presence' (in the presence of, 4 after) and in 1Cor 7:26 it is 'present' as in the present distress (2 after), different senses of the English word.

Suffering stands with the group in 2Ki 7:12 (hungry, 6 before), Luk 13:2 (suffered, 10 after) and 1Pe 4:1 (suffered, 2 and 2 after). In 1Pe 4:1 the suffering of Christ in the flesh is within two words of the way of thinking the readers are to arm themselves with.

Answering stands with the group in nine verses: four of Gen 18 (positions not stored), Gen 31:31 (6 before), Exo 2:14 (13 before), Est 4:13 (reply, 3 before), Luk 7:43 (1 before) and Luk 13:2 (2 before). In every verse the supposition is said within a spoken exchange of question and answer.

Peace stands with the group in 2Ki 20:19 (3 after), Isa 39:8 (2 after), Mat 10:34 (4 after, twice) and Luk 12:51 (4 after). The same word has two stances: Hezekiah supposes there will be peace in his days, and in Mat 10:34 and Luk 12:51 the supposition that Jesus came to bring peace is the one corrected.

Returning stands with the group in Jer 3:7 (5 after), Jer 40:5 (19 before) and Heb 11:15 (8 after). In Jer 3:7 the return is what was expected and did not happen; in Heb 11:15 it is what thinking of the land would have allowed.

Reward and its opposite stand with the group in Deu 15:9 ('unworthy', 1 before, by the code H1100I), Mat 22:17 (pay, 2 after, the tax) and Heb 10:29 (punishment, 1 before). In each verse the partner is within two words of the member; in Heb 10:29 the punishment is what the question asks the hearer to estimate.

The poor and the rich stand with the group in Deu 15:9 (poor, 10 after), Psa 40:17 (poor 3 and needy 2 before), Mic 2:8 (rich, 4 before) and Joh 13:29 (poor, 17 after); Eph 3:20 has 'abundantly' (6 before). In Psa 40:17, Deu 15:9 and Joh 13:29 the poor are the ones the thought is directed to: thought taken for them, an unworthy thought toward a poor brother, a supposed gift to the poor.

Righteousness and truth stand with the group in Gen 18:28 (righteous, position not stored, in the supposed case), Job 35:2 (just, 2 after), Mat 22:17 (lawful, 1 after), 2Cor 12:6 (truth, 5 before), Phili 4:8 (honorable 15 and just 13 before) and 1Ti 6:5 (truth, 1 before). In Job 35:2 and Mat 22:17 the member is the judgment whether something is just or lawful.

Searching and finding stand with the group in ten verses. In Gen 18:28 and Gen 18:30 'find' is the condition of each supposed number (positions not stored); in Mat 18:12 (17 after), Luk 2:44 (9 after) and Joh 20:15 the search follows or acts on the supposition; in Joh 5:39 the search of the Scriptures is 4 words before the supposition; in 1Ch 28:9 the Lord searches hearts (6 before) and 'seek' is 2 after.

Doing and serving stand with the group in twelve verses. 'Do' is the partner in nine: Gen 18:29 and 18:30 (positions not stored), Num 33:56 (1 after), Luk 12:17 (4 after), Rom 2:3 (7 after), Eze 18:14 (11 after), 1Cor 7:36 (10 after), Ecc 9:10 (5 before) and Eph 3:20 (8 before); in Num 33:56 and Luk 12:17 the doing is what is purposed or asked within 4 words of the thought. 'Serve' is the partner in 1Ch 28:9 (12 before), Joh 16:2 (service, 2 after, which the killer supposes he offers) and Phili 2:25 (minister, 16 after).

Giving stands with the group in twelve verses. It is within three words after the member in Jdg 15:2 (3), 1Sa 18:21 (1) and Luk 12:51 (3), where it is what is done or supposed on the strength of the thought (her father gave her away, Saul will give her to him, Jesus supposed to give peace); in the others it is 4 to 15 words away (Deu 15:9, 1Sa 18:17, Jer 3:19, Jer 40:5, Dan 7:25, Luk 8:18, Joh 13:29, Rom 12:3, 1Cor 13:11).

Sin stands with the group in Deu 15:9 (19 after), Eze 18:14 (sins, 5 after), Luk 13:2 (sinners, 5 after), 1Cor 7:36 (15 after) and 1Pe 4:1 (6 after). In Luk 13:2 and Eze 18:14 the sin is within the clause of what is supposed (whether they were worse sinners, the sins of the father seen by the son); in the other three it is in a later clause.

Taking stands with the group in seven verses. In Luk 8:18 (taken, 2 after) and Joh 20:15 (take, position not stored) the taking away is what follows the supposition about what a person has or where he is; in Act 8:20 'obtain' is 1 word after the member and is what Simon supposed he could do; in 2Cor 10:5 'take' is 2 before and acts on thought; in 2Sa 13:33 (4 before), 2Ki 7:12 (4 after) and Mat 17:25 (6 after) it is a different act.

Asking stands with the group in 2Sa 14:15 (request, 7 after), Mat 6:7 (pray, 6 before) and Mat 26:53 (appeal, 3 after). In Mat 6:7 those who pray suppose they will be heard for many words; in Mat 26:53 the supposition is whether Jesus cannot appeal to the Father; in 2Sa 14:15 the request is what the speaker came to make.

Affliction stands with the group in Lam 1:9 (affliction, 8 after), 1Cor 7:26 (distress, 3 after) and Phili 1:17 (afflict, 1 after). In Phili 1:17 the thought is of afflicting Paul and the affliction is 1 word after it; in 1Cor 7:26 the distress is the ground of the judgment; in Lam 1:9 the affliction is the speaker's lament.

Trust stands with the group in 1Sa 27:12 (trusted, 2 before), 2Ki 18:20 and Isa 36:5 (trust, 8 after) and Mic 2:8 (trustingly, 1 before). In 1Sa 27:12 the trust is the ground of Achish's thought; in the two parallel verses the question of whom they trust follows the supposed claim about words.

Cleanness and uncleanness stand with the group in 1Sa 20:26 (clean, 4 after, twice), Lam 1:9 (uncleanness, 5 before) and Rom 14:14 (unclean, 2 before, three nodes). In Rom 14:14 the uncleanness is the object of the thinking and depends on it; in 1Sa 20:26 Saul's thought is that David is not clean.

Wisdom and understanding stand with the group in eight verses. The partner is within two words in Pro 14:15 (prudent, 1 before), Psa 73:16 (understand, 1 after), Ecc 9:10 (wisdom, 2 after) and 1Cor 3:18 (wise, 2 after); in 1Cor 3:18 the person thinks that he is wise, so wisdom is what is thought of oneself. In 1Ch 28:9 (3 before), 2Sa 14:17 (12 after), Rom 2:3 (11 after) and 1Cor 7:40 (7 before) the partner is farther off.

Destruction stands with the group in Job 2:3 (destroy, 18 after), Psa 38:12 (ruin, 1 before) and Psa 119:78 (wronged, 3 before). In Psa 38:12 the ruin is 1 word before the meditating and the meditating is on treachery; in Psa 119:78 the speaker meditates after being wronged; in Job 2:3 the destroying is in a later clause.

Evil and the wicked stand with the group in Job 1:8 (evil, 12 after), Job 2:3 (evil, 13 after) and Pro 15:28 (wicked, 3 after). In Job the evil is what the one considered turns away from; in Pro 15:28 the wicked is set against the righteous whose heart ponders.

Fear stands with the group in Job 1:8 (fears, 9 after), Job 2:3 (10 after), Job 15:4 (fear, 2 before) and Mat 1:20 (14 after). In Job 1:8 and 2:3 the fear of God describes the one considered; in Job 15:4 fear of God and meditation are both what is being done away with.

Remembering stands with the group in Psa 63:6, Psa 77:3, Psa 77:6 and Psa 143:5, in every one 3 words before the member. The verses pair the remembering of God, a song or the days of old with the meditating that follows.

Precepts and authority stand with the group in Psa 119:15 (precepts, 1 after), Psa 119:27 (1 before), Psa 119:78 (2 after) and Mar 10:42 (exercise authority, 8 after). In the three Psalm verses the precepts are within two words of the meditating; in Mar 10:42 the member is the sense of those who are reputed rulers.

The heart stands with the group in five verses, within three words in every one: Psa 19:14 and Psa 49:3 (1 after, the meditation of the heart), Psa 77:6 (2 after), Pro 15:28 (2 before) and Luk 2:19 (3 after). The verses name the heart as the place of the meditating or pondering.

Works stand with the group in Psa 77:12 (work, 1 before), Psa 143:5 (work, 4 after), Psa 145:5 (works, 1 before) and Ecc 2:11 (toil, 4 after). In the three Psalm verses the works are God's and are the object of the meditating; in Ecc 2:11 the toil is the speaker's own.

Life and death stand with the group in Isa 53:8 (living, 5 after), Eze 18:28 (live, 8 after), Rom 4:19 (dead, 4 after) and Heb 11:19 (dead, 7 after). In Rom 4:19 and Heb 11:19 what is considered is a body as good as dead and God's power to raise the dead; in Eze 18:28 life is the outcome of considering and turning away.

Love stands with the group in Psa 119:48 (love, 1 before) and Psa 119:97 (3 before): in both the love of the commandments or the law comes just before the meditating on them. In Jos 7:21 the partner is covetousness (3 after) beside the surface 'weighing' as a weight of gold.

Searching stands with the group in Psa 38:12 (seek, 7 and 4 before), Psa 77:6 (search, 4 after) and Act 10:19 (looking for, 8 after). In Psa 77:6 the search follows the meditating in the same verse; in Psa 38:12 those who seek the speaker's hurt come before the meditating on treachery; in Act 10:19 the men looking for Peter are named after he is pondering.

Taking stands with the group in Gen 24:22 (took, 3 before), Jos 7:21 (took, 4 after), Eze 5:1 (take, 2 before) and Mat 1:20 (take, 15 after). In the first three the member is the weight of a thing taken (a ring, gold, balances), a measure and not a thought; only Mat 1:20, taking Mary as wife, belongs with the considering.

Wisdom and understanding stand with the group in seven verses. In Psa 77:12 (ponder, 3 before) and Psa 143:5 (ponder, 3 after) a second verb of musing is in the same clause as the member; in Psa 49:3 the meditation is between wisdom (1 before) and understanding (2 after); in Pro 17:28 the silent fool is considered wise (1 after) and intelligent (4 after); in Psa 119:27 understanding is 3 before, in Ecc 12:9 'wise' is 6 before and in Isa 53:8 'judgment' is 4 before.

Belief stands with the group in Act 19:9 (unbelief, 10 before), 1Th 3:5 (faith, 8 after), 1Th 3:7 (faith, 13 after) and 1Ti 1:16 (believe, 13 after). The three verses of 'for this reason' state the cause first and name faith or believing 8 to 13 words after; in Act 19:9 the reasoning follows the unbelief.

Words of duration stand with the group in Dan 4:34 (everlasting, 10 after), 1Ti 1:16 (eternal, 17 after) and 1Pe 3:15 (always, 7 before). The distances show the partner is in another clause of each verse, with no grammatical tie to the member.

Bearing stands with the group in Num 18:32 (bear, 2 before), 1Th 3:5 (bear, 2 after) and 1Ti 1:16 (patience, 9 after). In Num 18:32 and 1Th 3:5 the verb bear is in the same clause as the phrase of reason (bear no sin by reason of it; could bear it no longer).

Knowing stands with the group in Mar 12:24 (know, 2 after), Luk 9:47 (knowing, 1 before) and 1Th 3:5 (learn, 6 after). In Mar 12:24 the stated reason for the error is not knowing the Scriptures or the power of God; in Luk 9:47 Jesus' knowing stands 1 word before the reasoning in their hearts.

Sin stands with the group in Num 18:32 (sin, 1 before), Isa 1:18 (sins, 4 after) and 1Jo 3:8 (sinning, 9 and 3 before). In all three the sin is named near the reason: borne by reason of the offering, addressed in the reasoning together, and the ground of the appearing of the Son of God.

Hearing stands with the group in 2Ch 6:19 (listening, 8 after), Job 35:13 (hear, 4 before) and Act 28:22 (hear, 6 before). In Job 35:13 hearing and regarding are paired as what God does not do for an empty cry; in 2Ch 6:19 the regard asked for and the listening are asked together.

Works stand with the group in Exo 5:9 (work, 5 before; labor, 1 before), Psa 28:5 (works, 1 after; work, 3 after), Isa 5:12 (work, 5 after) and Lam 4:2 (work, 3 after). In Psa 28:5 and Isa 5:12 the Lord's works are what is not regarded; in Exo 5:9 the work is the burden laid on the men; in Lam 4:2 the work is a potter's hands.

Worthlessness and conceit stand with the group in 1Sa 1:16 (worthless, 2 after), 1Sa 25:25 (1 after) and Job 37:24 (conceit, 3 after). In the two Samuel verses regard is asked not to be given to a person as worthless; in Job 37:24 God does not regard those wise in their own conceit.
