Contempt stands with the group in Isa 33:8 (despised, 2 before), Act 28:22 (spoken against, 9 after) and 1Ti 6:1 (reviled, 11 after). In each verse a word of contempt is in the same sentence as the regard.

A bodily change stands with the group in Dan 5:6 (changed, 1 before), Dan 5:10 (change, 3 after) and Dan 7:28 (changed, 5 after). These are the three Aramaic verses in which the thoughts alarm the person, and the change of color is named within five words of the alarmed thoughts.

Evil and wickedness stand with the group in all fourteen verses, within five words of the member in each. Within one word: Pro 15:26, Mat 15:19, Mar 7:21 and Jam 2:4; within three: Gen 6:5, Job 21:27, Psa 10:4 and Psa 56:5; at four or five: Pro 12:5, Isa 55:7, Isa 59:7, Jer 4:14, Eze 38:10 and Mat 9:4. In Pro 12:5 the thoughts of the righteous are set beside the counsels of the wicked.

Fear and alarm stand with the group in six verses. In Dan 4:19, 5:6, 5:10 and 7:28 the thoughts are the subject of alarming, with the alarm 1 to 2 words after the member; in Job 32:6 the speaker is afraid, 4 words before declaring his opinion; in 2Cor 11:3 the fear (10 before) is Paul's fear about the readers' thoughts.

A heart or mind is named with the group in all fifteen verses. It is within three words of the member in eight (Gen 6:5, 1Ch 29:18, Dan 2:30, Luk 1:51, Eze 38:10, Mat 15:19, Luk 2:35, Heb 4:12), and in Rom 2:15 the conscience is 3 before; it is 4 to 9 away in Psa 139:23, Mar 7:21, Jer 4:14, Mat 9:4, Luk 5:22 and Dan 7:28. The verses place the thoughts in, or coming out of, the heart.

Intention stands with the group in Gen 6:5 (intention, 1 before), 1Ch 29:18 (purposes, 1 before), Mic 4:12 (plan, 4 after) and Heb 4:12 (intentions, 2 after). The partner words are of the same kind as the member and are paired with it in the verse.

Knowing stands with the group in sixteen verses. In thirteen the thoughts are the object of a verb of knowing or perceiving (within four words before the member where the position is stored: Job 21:27, Psa 94:11, Psa 139:2, Psa 139:23, Dan 2:30, Mic 4:12, Mat 9:4, Luk 5:22, Luk 6:8, Luk 11:17, 1Cor 2:11, 1Cor 3:20; Mat 12:25 has no stored position); the exceptions are Dan 2:29 (known, 7 after) and Mat 22:16 and Mar 12:14, where 'opinion' stands 14 and 9 words after 'know'.

Works stand with the group in Psa 92:5 (works, 3 before), Isa 66:18 (works, 1 before) and Rom 2:15 (work, 10 before). In Psa 92:5 and Isa 66:18 works and thoughts are paired within three words, as God's works and thoughts and as what the Lord knows of the nations.

Words of life stand with the group in Dan 2:30 (living, 9 before), Dan 5:10 (live, 3 before) and Heb 4:12 (living, 19 before). The distances, and the phrases (the living, live forever, the word is living), show no grammatical tie to the member.

Declaring stands with the group in six verses. In Job 32:6, 32:10 and 32:17 'declare' is 2 words before the member and the opinion is what is declared; in Psa 40:5 (proclaim, 4 after) and Isa 55:8 (declares, 4 after) the declaring follows the thoughts of the Lord; in Dan 5:10 (declared, 5 before) it is the queen's speech.

Answering stands with the group in five verses. In Job 20:2 (answer, 1 after) and Luk 5:22 (answered, 1 after) the thoughts are the occasion of the answer, and in Dan 4:19 (answered, 3 after, twice) the king answers after the thoughts alarmed him; in Job 32:6 (12 before) and Job 32:17 (6 before) the answer comes before the opinion is declared.

Wealth stands with the group in Pro 18:11 (wealth, 6 before), Ecc 10:20 (rich, 7 after) and Isa 55:7 (abundantly, 8 after). In Pro 18:11 the imagination is the wall around the rich man's wealth; the other two partners are in later clauses with no grammatical tie.

Righteousness stands with the group in Pro 12:5 (righteous, 1 after; just, 2 after), and the partner is sexual immorality in Mat 15:19 (3 after) and Mar 7:21 (1 after), in the list that follows 'evil thoughts', and 'lawful' in Mar 12:14 (8 after). In Pro 12:5 the thoughts of the righteous are set beside the counsels of the wicked.

Teaching stands with the group in Pro 12:5 (counsels, 3 after), Mat 22:16 (teach, 9 before) and Mar 12:14 (teach, 5 after). In the two Gospel verses the opinion in question is the opinion of persons, which the Teacher is said not to regard while he teaches the way of God.

Wisdom and discernment stand with the group in six verses. In Psa 139:2 (discern, 1 before) and Heb 4:12 (discerning, 1 before) the thoughts are the object of discerning; in 1Cor 3:20 (wise, 1 after) the thoughts are of the wise and are futile; in Pro 18:2 (understanding, 6 before), Mic 4:12 (understand, 3 after) and Dan 2:30 (wisdom, 13 before) the partner is farther off.
Calling stands with the group in Isa 7:14 (call, 3 after), Mat 1:23 (5 after) and Luk 1:31 (7 after). In all three the calling of the child's name follows the conceiving and the bearing of a son.

Bearing stands with the group in six verses, 1 word after the member in Jdg 13:3, 13:5, 13:7 and Isa 7:14, 2 after in Mat 1:23 and 4 after in Luk 1:31. In every verse the bearing of a child is the second act of the pair, conceive and bear.

The surface 'imagines' carries two codes in 1Cor 8:2: G1380, the verb 'to think, suppose', which gives the sense, and G1161, the connective 'but, now', which the unit aligns into the same word. Only the verb is a word of supposing; the connective was read for what it does in the sentence at stage 1.

The surface 'suppose' carries eight codes in three senses. A case put forward: H0194 'perhaps' in Gen 18:28-32 (five times) and H2009 'behold' in Eze 18:14. A supposition held: H0559 'to say in one's heart' in 2Sa 13:32 and 2Sa 13:33, G5274 in Luk 7:43 and Act 2:15, G3633 in Joh 21:25 and Jam 1:7, G5282 in Act 13:25 and G1380 in Jam 4:5. The connective G1161 in Rom 2:3, which does not carry either sense.

The surface 'supposing' carries two codes, G3543 (Luk 2:44, Act 14:19, Act 16:27) and G1380 (Joh 11:31, Joh 20:15, Act 27:13). Both are verbs of thinking and give the same sense, a supposition on which the people act; the surface has no second sense.

The surface 'think' carries seventeen codes in four senses. A judgment or supposition held: G1380 (20 verses), G3543 (4), G5426 (4), G3049 (Phili 4:8 and 2Cor 12:6), G3539 (Eph 3:20), H2803J (6), H1819 (Est 4:13). A thing said or claimed: H0559 (2Ki 18:20, 2Ch 13:8, Isa 36:5, Eze 11:5). The idiom 'in the eyes of': H5869I (Num 36:6, 2Sa 10:3, 1Ch 19:3, Jer 40:5). Other acts of mind: H7200H (2Sa 18:27, a judgment from seeing), H2142 (Psa 119:52, to call to mind), H2803I (Isa 10:7, to plan), H5452 (Dan 7:25, to intend), G1760 (Mat 9:4). H0413 (Jer 40:4, a preposition) and G1161 with G2233 (2Pe 1:13, a connective and the verb of counting) sit in the unit without carrying the sense.

The surface 'thinking' carries nine codes in three senses. A thought held or quoted: H0559 (eight verses, with the purpose of 2Ch 32:1), G1380 (2Cor 12:19) and G3633 (Phili 1:17). The mind or way of thinking as a noun: G5424 (1Cor 14:20), G1771 (1Pe 4:1) and G1261 (Rom 1:21). Calling to mind: G3421 (Heb 11:15). H0853 (Neh 6:9, the object marker) and G2532 (Rom 1:21, a connective) sit in the units without carrying a sense.

The surface 'thinks' carries four codes: H0559 (1Sa 20:3, a thought quoted), G1380 (seven verses, a person's estimate of himself), G3049 (Rom 14:14, reckoning a thing unclean) and G3543 (1Cor 7:36, a judgment of his conduct). All four are verbs of holding a view; the surface has one sense with four verbs behind it.

The surface 'thought' carries twenty-eight codes in five senses. A thought quoted or a supposition: H0559 (25 verses, in three uses at stage 1: thought quoted, assumption, and intention), G1380 (5), G3543 (2), H2803J (2), H1819 (3), G1260 with G3004G (Luk 12:17) and G5426 (1Cor 13:11). A plan or purpose: H2803I (1Sa 18:25, Psa 40:17), G2233 (2Cor 9:5, Phili 2:25). Thought as a noun: H4284 (1Ch 28:9), H6248 (Job 12:5), H2808 (Ecc 9:10), H7808 (Amo 4:13), G3540 (2Cor 10:5), H1697G with H1961 (Deu 15:9). Giving heed and calling to mind: H0995 (Pro 14:15, Pro 21:29) and H2142 (Lam 1:9). Reputation and standing given: G3141 (1Ti 3:7, well thought of), G2919 (Act 26:8) and H5869I (2Sa 3:19, in the eyes of). Small words sit in some units without carrying a sense: H3588A, H1931, H0834A, H0194 and H7725G (Mic 2:8, the returning).

The surface 'considered' carries seventeen codes in two senses and some small words. Attention given to a matter: H7760K with H3820A (the idiom of setting the heart, Job 1:8 and 2:3, and Pro 24:32 with H7896K), H6437G (Ecc 2:11), H7200H (Eze 18:28), H7878 (Isa 53:8), H7920 (Dan 7:8), G1760 (Mat 1:20) and G2657 (Rom 4:19). Reckoning or being reckoned: H2803H (1Ki 10:21, 2Ch 9:20, Neh 13:13), H2803J (Pro 17:28), G2233 (Heb 11:11, Heb 11:26), G3049 (Heb 11:19) and G1380 in the sense of being reputed (Mar 10:42). H1934 (Dan 7:8, a verb of being), H0595 (Pro 24:32, the pronoun I) and G3756 (Rom 4:19, a negator) sit in the units without carrying either sense.

The surface 'meditate' carries three codes in three senses. Musing on a named object: H1897 (Jos 1:8, Psa 63:6, Psa 143:5), H7878 (nine Psalm verses, with Psa 77:3 as a complaint) and H7742 (Gen 24:63, the lexicon marks the meaning uncertain). Devising harm: H1897 in Psa 38:12, where the object is treachery. The same surface therefore gives a musing on God and the law, a complaint, and a plotting.

The surface 'meditation' carries five codes: H7881 (Job 15:4, Psa 119:97, Psa 119:99), H1902H (Psa 19:14), H1900 (Psa 49:3), H7879 (Psa 104:34) and H5921A (Psa 104:34, the preposition 'upon'). The four nouns give one sense, the inner musing; H7879 also lists 'complaint' in the lexicon but not in this verse.

The surface 'pondering' carries two codes, G4820 (Luk 2:19, to throw together, ponder) and G1760 (Act 10:19, to reflect on). The two Greek verbs give one sense, a sustained reflection on named things.

The surface 'ponders' carries two codes in two senses. H6424 in Pro 5:21 is the Lord's weighing of a man's paths, and H1897 in Pro 15:28 is a person's going over how to answer. The stored sense head of H6424 reads 'to envy' and disagrees with its lexicon range, flagged in #2533.

The surface 'weigh' carries three codes in two senses. Weighing out as a physical act: H8254 (Ezr 8:29, the vessels weighed before the priests) and H5187 (Zep 1:11, traders laden with silver). Weighing up what is said: G1252 (1Cor 14:29).

The surface 'weighing' carries two codes in two senses. H4948 (four occurrences in Gen 24:22 twice, Jos 7:21 and Eze 5:1) is a weight, a measure of shekels; H0239 in Ecc 12:9 is the Preacher weighing proverbs with care.

The surface 'reason' carries eighteen codes in four senses and some small words. The ground or cause: G0156 (Act 10:21, 28:18, 28:20, 2Ti 1:6), G1223 and G5124 (Mar 12:24, 1Th 3:5, 1Th 3:7, 1Ti 1:16, 1Jo 3:8), G5484 (Eph 3:1, 3:14), G1352 (Rom 15:22), G1519 (1Jo 3:8), H1697M (Jos 5:4, 1Ki 11:27), H5921A (Num 18:32, 1Sa 20:29), H3651C (1Sa 20:29), H6440I (Gen 41:31, 47:13), H2600 (Job 1:9, Pro 3:30). Reasoning with someone: H3198 (Isa 1:18). Understanding as a faculty: G2138 (Jam 3:17, open to reason), H4486 (Dan 4:34, 4:36, reason returned). An account given: G3056 (1Pe 3:15). G2596 and G0302 (Act 18:14) and H1961 (Eze 19:10, the copula, flagged in #2533) sit in the units without carrying these senses.
The surface 'reasoned' carries two codes in two senses: G1256 (five verses, Paul reasoning with hearers in speech) and G3049 (1Cor 13:11, the reckoning of a child).

The surface 'reasoning' carries two codes in two senses: G1261 in Luk 9:47, the reasoning inside the disciples' hearts, and G1256 in Act 19:8 and Act 19:9, Paul's reasoning aloud in the synagogue and the hall. The same word gives an inward reasoning and a spoken one.

The surface 'regard' carries twenty-seven codes in five senses and some small words. Looking on and heeding: H8159 (three verses), H5027 (three), H7200G (two), H7789, H6485I, H6437G (two), H7919A and H0995. Acknowledging or knowing: H3045 (three), H5234A, G1097 and G6063. Favour: H5375Q (2Ki 3:14). Counting as: H2803H (two), G3049 (two), G2233 (two), H5414I (1Sa 1:16) and H6188 (Lev 19:23). 'With regard to': G4012 (Act 28:22), G3313 (Col 2:16), H1700 (Ecc 3:18) and H9006 (Jdg 15:3). H8104J (2Ch 5:11) gives observing a rule. The negators H0408 and H3808 (Exo 5:9, Job 9:21), the object marker H0853 and H3820A (1Sa 25:25, heart in an idiom) sit in the units without carrying a sense of their own.

The surface 'regarded' carries four codes: H2803H (Gen 31:15, Psa 44:22, Lam 4:2, Hos 8:12), H2803J (Isa 29:16, 29:17) and G3049 (Rom 2:26, 8:36), all 'counted as'; and G1380 in Luk 22:24, which is being reputed or reckoned greatest. The surface has one sense with a reputation sense in one verse.

The surface 'imagination' carries two codes in two senses. H4906 (Pro 18:11) is a figure or conceit in which the rich man pictures his wealth as a wall, and G1761 (Act 17:29) is a device of thought that shapes an image.

The surface 'opinion' carries three codes in three senses. H1843 (Job 32:6, 32:10, 32:17) is a view or knowledge that Elihu declares; H3820A (Pro 18:2) is the heart, what the fool lays bare; G0991 (Mat 22:16, Mar 12:14) is a looking at persons, regard for how they appear.

The surface 'thoughts' carries fifteen codes, all nouns of the same kind: thought and device (H4284, 19 verses; H4209; H7454; H7476; H4093; H8312; G1761; G3540; G1270), reasoning (G1261, seven verses; G3053), the mind (G1271), disquietings (H5587B), the muttered musing of enemies (H1902H in Lam 3:62), matters that come up (H1697I in Eze 38:10) and the article G3588 in 1Cor 2:11, whose morph is empty and which is flagged in #2533. The surface has one sense; the verses differ in whose thoughts they are, a person's, the wicked's or the Lord's.

The surface 'conceive' carries nine codes in two senses, with one rhetorical use between them. The bodily conceiving of a child: H2232 (Num 5:28), H2029 (Jdg 13:3), H2030A (Jdg 13:5, 13:7, Isa 7:14), H3179 (Psa 51:5), and the Greek G4815 (Luk 1:31), G2192 with G1722 (Mat 1:23) and G2602 with G4690G (Heb 11:11). The figurative conceiving of trouble, chaff and mischief: H2029 in Job 15:35, Isa 33:11 and Isa 59:4, where what is conceived is borne as evil or stubble. H2029 in Num 11:12 is Moses' rhetorical question whether he conceived the whole people, the bodily word used of his relation to them.

The surface 'imagine' carries two codes: H2803I in Psa 41:7, which gives the sense (to devise the worst against the speaker), and H5921A, the preposition 'upon', which the unit aligns into the same word without carrying a sense.

Qualifiers stand with the supposing group in 58 verses with negators (79 stored pairs) and in many more with adjectives and adverbs. The negator reaches the member itself, forbidding, denying or withholding the supposition, in Mat 5:17, Mat 10:34 and Joh 5:45 (do not think, 1 word before), Act 17:29, Jam 1:7, 2Cor 11:16, 2Sa 13:32 and 2Sa 13:33, Rom 12:3 (not to think too highly of oneself), Isa 10:7 and Lam 1:9. In Jos 22:28, 1Sa 20:26, 2Sa 5:6, Neh 6:9, Mat 26:53, Joh 11:56, Act 13:25, Luk 12:17 and Jon 1:6 the negator is inside the supposed or quoted content and reaches another word of it. In Mat 6:7, 1Cor 14:20, Act 12:9, Phili 1:17, Rom 1:21, 1Cor 8:2, Jam 1:26, Eze 20:32 and Act 2:15 it stands in the same sentence and reaches another verb (heap up, be children, know, sincerely, honor, know, bridle, happen, drunk); adjacency is not scope. Of the adjectives and adverbs, the ones that qualify the supposing itself are 'again' (Gen 18:32), 'now' (2Ch 13:8), 'so' (Isa 10:7, Eze 11:5), 'all along' (2Cor 12:19) and 'otherwise' (Phili 3:15); most of the rest, such as wise, unclean, religious, incredible and necessary, qualify the state of affairs that is supposed.

Qualifiers stand with the attending group in five verses with negators (6 stored pairs). Only in 1Ki 10:21 is the member negated (silver not reckoned as anything). In Jos 1:8 the negator reaches 'depart' (the Book shall not depart), in Eze 18:28 it reaches 'die', in Mat 1:20 it reaches 'fear' (13 words after) and in Rom 4:19 it reaches 'weaken' (not the considering). Of the adjectives and adverbs only 'day', after the meditating in Jos 1:8 and Psa 1:2, qualifies the act itself (when it is done); 'wise' and 'fool' (Pro 17:28) and 'faithful' (Heb 11:11) describe the one considered, and 'righteous' (Pro 15:28) the one whose heart ponders.

Qualifiers stand with the reasoning group in five verses with negators (14 stored pairs). In Pro 3:30 the negator reaches 'reason' in 'for no reason' (the ground is denied) and in Act 28:18 'no reason for the death penalty' does the same; in Mar 12:24 the 'not' of the question reaches 'the reason' (is this not the reason), and 'neither ... nor' reaches 'know'; in Num 18:32 the negator reaches 'bear' (bear no sin by reason of it); in 1Sa 20:29 it reaches 'come' after the reason is stated; in Gen 41:31 the negation is in 'unknown'. Of the adjectives, 'three' (Act 17:2) gives the length of the reasoning, 'like a child' (1Cor 13:11) its manner, and 'often' (Rom 15:22) the repetition of the hindering.

One qualifier stands with the group of the mind's set, the negator in Mar 8:33. It is 1 word before 'setting your mind' and reaches it: Peter is not setting his mind on the things of God, and the verse gives the opposite object, the things of man. The stored data holds no adjective or adverb for this group; in Rom 8:5 and Rom 8:6 the contrast is carried by the nouns flesh and Spirit, not by a qualifier.

Qualifiers stand with the taking-account group in 19 verses with negators (33 stored pairs). The negator reaches the member, denying the regard, in Gen 4:5, Deu 33:9, 1Sa 25:25, Job 34:27, Job 35:13, Job 37:24, Psa 28:5, Isa 5:12, Isa 13:17, Isa 33:8, Lam 4:16, 2Th 3:15 and, as 'no longer', 2Cor 5:16; in Gen 31:15 and Rom 2:26 it is in a question about being counted as. It reaches another word in Lev 19:23 (not eaten), Psa 28:5 (build no more) and Col 2:16 (let no one pass judgment). The adjectives that matter are the complements of status after 'regarded' and 'regard': foreigners (Gen 31:15), a strange thing (Hos 8:12), the greatest (Luk 22:24), servants (1Cor 4:1).

Qualifiers stand with the group of what the mind holds in 12 verses with negators (20 stored pairs) and many adjectives. The negator reaches 'seek' in Psa 10:4, 'care' in Mat 22:16 and Mar 12:14 (the opinion is what is not cared about), 'know' in Mic 4:12 (they do not know the thoughts of the Lord), 'curse' in Ecc 10:20, 'think' in Act 17:29 and the sameness of the two thoughts in Isa 55:8 (my thoughts are not your thoughts). The adjective qualifies the thoughts directly in 'evil' (Mat 15:19, Mar 7:21, Jam 2:4), 'wicked' (Jer 4:14) and 'very deep' (Psa 92:5); in 'the thoughts of the righteous' and 'of the wicked' (Pro 12:5, Pro 15:26) the adjective names whose thoughts they are.

Qualifiers stand with the devising group in four verses with negators (5 stored pairs). They reach words other than the member: 'defiled' in Num 5:28 (a woman not defiled shall conceive), 'borne' in Jdg 13:3 (barren, has not borne), and in Jdg 13:5 and 13:7 the things the woman must not do (a razor, wine, strong drink, unclean food). The adjectives are 'barren' (Jdg 13:3), 'clean' (Num 5:28) and 'faithful' (Heb 11:11, the one who promised); none qualifies the conceiving itself.

Entities are named in 89 of the 155 verses of the supposing group, 62 different ones in 187 stored pairs (118 human, 69 divine). The divine are God (31), the Lord (21), Jesus (8), Christ (5), the Most High and the possessive forms. The human are mostly the figures of the narratives who think or suppose: David (19), Saul (8), Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Hanun, Hezekiah, Naaman, Esther, Mordecai, Judas and many others, with man, men and brothers. This group names far more persons than any other group of thought (the next largest has 25 different entities); the other groups name God, the Lord and Jesus, and a few persons each.

Entities are named in 25 of the 52 verses of the attending group, 25 different ones in 59 stored pairs (37 human, 22 divine). The divine are the Lord (12), God (8), Jesus and Christ. The human are mostly the persons considered or doing the considering: the servant Job (4 with 'servant'), Solomon, Sarah, Isaac, Elijah, the priests Shelemiah, Zadok and Pedaiah, and 'man'. Unlike the supposing group, the persons here are the objects of the attention in Job 1:8, 2:3 and Neh 13:13, or the speakers who meditate on God.

Entities are named in 18 of the 35 verses of the reasoning group, 13 different ones in 30 stored pairs (12 human, 18 divine). The divine are God (7), Jesus (5), the Lord (4) and Christ (2); the human are the brothers, Joshua, Job, Solomon, David, Nebuchadnezzar, the disciples, man and men. Paul, who does the reasoning in the Acts verses, is not among the stored entities.

Entities are named in 1 of the 3 verses of the group of the mind's set: Mar 8:33 names the disciples (Jesus' disciples) and God and man (the things of God, the things of man), 3 stored pairs. Rom 8:5 and Rom 8:6 name no entity; the contrast there is flesh and Spirit. The group is too small to compare with the others except that God is named in it as in all of them.

Entities are named in 25 of the 43 verses of the taking-account group, 23 different ones in 54 stored pairs (34 human, 20 divine). The divine are God (8), the Lord (7), Christ (4) and the Almighty; the human include Nabal (4), man and men, the priests, Cain, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Elisha, Jehoshaphat, Samson, servants and brothers. Persons here are the ones regarded or not regarded (Nabal, Jehoshaphat, Cain's offering), and God is both the one who regards (Lam 4:16, Psa 80:14) and the one whose works are not regarded (Psa 28:5, Isa 5:12).

Entities are named in 28 of the 52 verses of the group of what the mind holds, 18 different ones in 49 stored pairs (21 human, 28 divine). The divine are God (12), the Lord (11), Jesus (2) and Christ; the human are man (6), Belteshazzar and Daniel (the Aramaic verses), Elihu, Abraham, Isaac, Eve, the disciples and 'person'. Here the divine pairs outnumber the human (28 to 21), as they do in the reasoning group (18 to 12) and not in the supposing, attending, taking-account or devising groups, where the human outnumber the divine; in this group many verses have God or Jesus knowing or declaring thoughts (Psa 94:11, Psa 139:2, Mat 9:4, Luk 5:22).

Entities are named in 8 of the 13 verses of the devising group, 7 different ones in 15 stored pairs (9 human, 6 divine). The divine are God (4), the Lord and Jesus; the human are Immanuel (3), Sarah (2), the woman and the child. The persons are those conceiving or conceived (Sarah, the woman, Immanuel), and the divine appear as the one who sends the angel or whose name 'God with us' the child bears.

The direction of the supposing changes across the verses. In most the supposer is a named person who holds a view about another person or a state of affairs: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Saul, David, Naaman and Hezekiah hold a quoted thought, with the human entity before the member in 72 of 118 human pairs. In Mat 17:25, Mat 18:12, Mat 21:28, Mat 22:17, Mat 22:42 and Luk 10:36 the direction is reversed: Jesus asks the hearer what he thinks. Toward God it runs in Psa 50:21 (you thought I was like yourself), Act 17:29 and Jon 1:6 (perhaps the god will give a thought to us), and from the Lord to the people in Eze 11:5.

The direction of the attending changes across the verses. In Jos 1:8, Psa 63:6, Psa 119:15 and Psa 143:5 it runs from the speaker to God, the law and God's works; in Job 1:8 and 2:3 it runs from the Lord to Satan concerning Job (have you considered my servant); in Mat 1:20 and Luk 2:19 a person turns the events over inwardly; in Heb 11:11 Sarah considers God faithful. The attention goes both from a person to God and from God to a person.

The direction of the reasoning changes across the verses. In Act 17:2, 17:17, 18:4, 18:19, 19:8 and 24:25 it runs from Paul to his hearers; in Mar 12:24 from Jesus to those he answers, with the ground of their error stated; in Isa 1:18 from the Lord to the people; in 1Ti 1:16 the ground runs from God to Paul (mercy received for this reason) and in 1Jo 3:8 the ground of the Son of God's appearing is stated; in Luk 9:47 Jesus knows the reasoning of the disciples' hearts.

The direction does not change across the verses of the group of the mind's set. In Rom 8:5 and Rom 8:6 the mind is set toward the flesh or toward the Spirit, and in Mar 8:33 toward the things of God or of man; in every verse the set is a direction toward an object, with an opposite named beside it. The only entities, in Mar 8:33, are the disciples (Jesus' disciples, whom he sees as he rebukes Peter) and God and man as what the mind is set toward.

The direction of the regard changes across the verses. It runs from a person to a person in 1Sa 25:25, 1Sa 1:16, 2Ki 3:14, Jer 24:5 and Pro 12:10 (the righteous regards his beast); from a person to God's works in Psa 28:5 and Isa 5:12; from God to a person in Gen 4:5 (no regard for Cain), Lam 4:16 and Job 37:24; asked of God in Psa 74:20, Psa 80:14 and 2Ch 6:19 (that he have regard for the covenant, the vine and the prayer); and withheld by God in Job 35:13 (he does not regard an empty cry). The status counted as runs from a speaker to the one counted in Gen 31:15, Psa 44:22, Isa 29:16 and Rom 8:36.

The direction of the thoughts changes across the verses. From the heart outward in Mat 15:19 and Mar 7:21 (evil thoughts come out of the heart); inward to a knower in Psa 94:11, Psa 139:2, Mat 9:4, Luk 5:22, Luk 6:8 and 1Cor 3:20 (the Lord or Jesus knows the thoughts of persons); from God to persons in Psa 40:5 (his thoughts toward us), Isa 55:8 and Mic 4:12 (his thoughts not known by those addressed); and from a person's own thoughts upon himself in Dan 4:19, Dan 5:6 and Dan 7:28 (his thoughts alarmed him).

The direction does not change across the verses of the devising group. In Jdg 13:3, 13:5, 13:7, Isa 7:14, Mat 1:23 and Luk 1:31 a messenger or the Lord announces to a woman that she will conceive and bear a son, and in Heb 11:11 Sarah received power to conceive; the conceiving runs from the woman to the child, and the divine entity is the source of the announcement.

In Rom 8:5 the mind is directed: those who live by the flesh and those who live by the Spirit each set their minds on the things of their own way. The act is a setting of the mind toward an object, stated as done by persons of either way of living, with the same verb for both.

In Rom 8:6 the setting of the mind is stated as the mind-set itself (the noun G5427, twice): a mind-set of the flesh and a mind-set of the Spirit. The verse gives the operation once for each side of the contrast and states what each issues in.

In Mar 8:33 the setting of the mind is negated for Peter: the negator stands 1 word before the verb and reaches it, so the act toward the things of God is stated as not being done, with the things of man as what the mind is on instead.
In Rom 8:5 and Rom 8:6 the setting of the mind is a pursuit of its object: the mind is directed toward the flesh or toward the Spirit, and the verses set the two against each other as alternatives.
In Mar 8:33 the act is a refusal as the verse states it: the setting of the mind on the things of God is negated and its opposite object is named in the same sentence.

The object of the setting is named in each verse as one of a pair of opposites: the things of the flesh against the things of the Spirit (Rom 8:5), the flesh against the Spirit (Rom 8:6), the things of God against the things of man (Mar 8:33). The direction does not change in kind across the three verses; only the pair differs.

In Rom 8:5 and Rom 8:6 the setting of the mind stands beside a way of living and its issue: living by the flesh or the Spirit goes with the mind-set, and the verse states death for the one and life and peace for the other. No entity is named in these two verses; the contrast is carried by the nouns flesh and Spirit.

Mar 8:33 is a rebuke: Jesus turns, sees his disciples, and says it to Peter. The setting of the mind is therefore named in a speech of correction aimed at one person in the hearing of the others, and the entities the stored data names in the verse are the disciples, God and man.

Regard is given as a done act in 2Ki 3:14 (Elisha has regard for Jehoshaphat), Pro 12:10 (the righteous man's care for his beast), Psa 144:3 (the Lord regards man) and 2Cor 5:16 (Christ once regarded according to the flesh). The act is a taking account of a person or a creature, and the subjects are a prophet, a righteous man, the Lord and the apostles.

Regard and its counting-as are foreseen in Jer 24:5 (the Lord will regard the exiles as good), Isa 29:17 (the fruitful field shall be counted as a forest) and Rom 2:26 (the uncircumcised will be counted as circumcision). The act stands in the future and gives a standing that does not yet hold.

Regard is asked or commanded in Psa 74:20, Psa 80:14 and 2Ch 6:19 (that the Lord have regard for the covenant, the vine and the prayer) and in 1Ti 6:1 and 1Cor 4:1 (that bondservants regard their masters as worthy, that the apostles be taken as servants). The act is put as what should be done, by God in the first three and by persons in the last two.

Regard is negated in thirteen verses: Gen 4:5, Deu 33:9, 1Sa 25:25, Job 34:27, Job 35:13, Job 37:24, Psa 28:5, Isa 5:12, Isa 13:17, Isa 33:8, Lam 4:16, 2Th 3:15 and Exo 5:9. The negator reaches the member in each (no regard, do not regard, nor does he regard), and the subjects are Cain's rival, the Levite, a lord, the wicked, God and the feasters, so the denial runs both from persons and from God.

In these thirteen verses the act is a refusal as the grammar states it: the regard is withheld from an offering, a person, the Lord's works, silver, man or a prayer. The refusal is spoken of God in Gen 4:5, Job 35:13, Job 37:24 and Lam 4:16, and of persons in the others.

Where regard is given or asked, the act is a pursuit of its object: the Lord is asked to look to the covenant, the vine and the prayer, Elisha acts out of regard for Jehoshaphat, and the righteous cares for his beast. The pursuit runs from persons to God's works and to persons, and from God to persons.

What the regard is directed at differs by verse: the Lord's works and deeds (Psa 28:5, Isa 5:12), the covenant, the vine and the prayer (Psa 74:20, Psa 80:14, 2Ch 6:19), persons (Nabal in 1Sa 25:25, Jehoshaphat in 2Ki 3:14, the exiles in Jer 24:5, the parents in Deu 33:9), Cain's offering (Gen 4:5), an empty cry (Job 35:13) and the self-wise (Job 37:24). Persons and the works of God are the commonest objects.

After 'regarded' and 'regard' the complement gives the standing: foreigners (Gen 31:15), a strange thing (Hos 8:12), the greatest (Luk 22:24), worthy of honor (1Ti 6:1). Each complement is a qualifier of the counting or regarding, naming what the person or thing is counted as.

The negator is a qualifier of the regard it reaches, turning the act into a denial: 'no' in Gen 4:5, 'not' in Job 37:24 and Psa 28:5 and Isa 5:12, 'no' in Isa 13:17 and Isa 33:8 and Lam 4:16. In each verse the negator is 1 word before or after the member and the verse states what it reaches.

Regard is bound up with worth in three verses: it is asked not to be given to a woman or a man as worthless (1Sa 1:16, 1Sa 25:25) and God does not give it to those wise in their own conceit (Job 37:24). The worth or the conceit of the person regarded is named in the same sentence, within three words of the member.

A word of contempt stands in the same sentence as the regard in Isa 33:8 (despised, 2 before), Act 28:22 (spoken against, 9 after) and 1Ti 6:1 (reviled, 11 after). The regard is set in a verse that also names the low standing of a city, a sect or a name.

Hearing and regard are paired in 2Ch 6:19 (listening, 8 after), Job 35:13 (hear, 4 before) and Act 28:22 (hear, 6 before): the regard is asked or denied together with a hearing, of a prayer, an empty cry or the views of a sect.

The surface 'regard' also holds the prepositional idiom 'with regard to' in Act 28:22 (G4012), Col 2:16 (G3313), Ecc 3:18 (H1700) and Jdg 15:3 (H9006): these are not an act of taking account of anyone and are read in their verses as standalone. The negators H0408 and H3808 in Exo 5:9 and Job 9:21 are aligned into the unit of the surface and are read as negators, not as acts of regard.

Reasoning is a done act of speech in seven Acts verses: Paul reasons in the synagogue, in the marketplace, in the hall of Tyrannus and before Felix (Act 17:2, 17:17, 18:4, 18:19, 19:8, 19:9, 24:25). The verb stands in the aorist or imperfect and is spoken to hearers, with persuading beside it in several; it is an exchange of grounds in speech and not a silent act.

In Luk 9:47 the reasoning is inward: it is in the hearts of the disciples after their dispute, and it is Jesus who knows it, the knowing standing 1 word before the member. The same noun therefore gives an unspoken reasoning here and the spoken reasoning of the Acts verses.
In 1Cor 13:11 the reckoning is the working out of a child and is set among speaking and thinking as one of the ways of a child; the verb is a past tense and is given up when the speaker became a man.

What the reasoning is on, where the verses give it, is the Scriptures in Act 17:2, the topics of righteousness, self-control and judgment before Felix in Act 24:25 and the kingdom of God in Act 19:8; the objects are matters of teaching put to hearers, with persuading as the aim in Act 18:4, 19:8.

In the ground phrases 'for this reason' and 'the reason why' (G1223, G5124, G5484, G1352, G0156) the member names the ground on which an act or state stands: Paul's sending to learn of faith (1Th 3:5), the comfort he received (1Th 3:7), the mercy received (1Ti 1:16), his imprisonment and prayer (Eph 3:1, Eph 3:14), his hindering (Rom 15:22), the chain he wears (Act 28:20) and the reminder to Timothy (2Ti 1:6). In each the ground is stated first and what rests on it follows, 8 to 13 words later where the stored positions are given.

The ground is set beside bearing and sin in four verses: sin is not borne by reason of the offering (Num 18:32), Paul could bear it no longer and sent (1Th 3:5), the sins are what the reasoning together addresses (Isa 1:18), and the Son of God appeared on the ground of the devil's sinning (1Jo 3:8). The reasoning or the ground is thus named where a burden or a sin stands within a few words.

Knowing is stated as the ground of error in Mar 12:24: the ground of the error is a lack of knowledge, of the Scriptures and of God's power, and the negator reaches the knowing. In Luk 9:47 the knowing is Jesus' knowing of the disciples' reasoning. The ground and the knowing stand within two words of each other in both verses.

The ground is denied in four verses: 'for no reason' (Job 1:9, Pro 3:30), no reason for the death penalty (Act 28:18) and the question whether this is not the reason (Mar 12:24). The negator reaches the reason itself in the first three, so the ground is stated as absent; in Mar 12:24 the question puts it as the answer.

Where the ground is denied (Job 1:9, Pro 3:30, Act 28:18) the act is a refusal of a ground: Satan asks whether Job fears God for nothing, the proverb forbids contending without cause, and the Romans found no ground for the penalty.

Two qualifiers give the reasoning its manner and length: 'three' Sabbath days in Act 17:2 (2 words before) gives how long it went on, and 'like a child' in 1Cor 13:11 (1 before and 2 after) gives the kind of reckoning. The qualifier of the ground in Rom 15:22 is 'often', which gives the repeated hindering the reason accounts for.

Reasoning and the ground run in different directions across the verses: from Paul to hearers in the Acts verses, from Jesus to those he answers in Mar 12:24, from the Lord to the people in Isa 1:18, and from God to Paul in 1Ti 1:16, where mercy is received for this reason. God and Jesus are named more often than any human in these verses, and Paul, who reasons in the Acts verses, is not among the stored entities.

Three words in the units of 'reason' do not carry the sense of the group: the copula H1961 in Eze 19:10 (flagged in #2533), the function words G2596 and G0302 in Act 18:14 and the adjective G2138 in Jam 3:17 ('open to reason', compliant). They are read as standalone in their verses; the causal phrase 'for this reason', which makes up most of the surface 'reason', is a ground and not a thought, which the double-meaning observation records.

Attending is a done act of musing on a named matter in Psa 1:2, Psa 63:6, Psa 143:5, Gen 24:63 and Pro 15:28 (how to answer), and of pondering in Luk 2:19, Act 10:19 and Mat 1:20 (the vision, these things). The verbs of musing and pondering are the same kind of act across the codes: a going over of something present to the mind, kept in the heart in Luk 2:19 and Pro 15:28.

The psalmist's meditating is foreseen as a resolve in Psa 77:12, Psa 119:15, 119:23, 119:27, 119:48, 119:78, 119:148 and Psa 145:5 (I will meditate). In seven of these the object is the Lord's precepts, statutes, promise, works or deeds, within two words of the member; the act is a purposed going over of what God has said or done.

Attending is commanded in Jos 1:8 (the Book of the Law is to be meditated on day and night) and in 1Cor 14:29 (the others are to weigh what the prophets say). The negator of Jos 1:8 reaches 'depart' (the Book shall not depart from the mouth), so the command to meditate stands beside a command that the Law not depart.

The Lord's own attending is stated in Job 1:8 and Job 2:3 (the Lord asks Satan whether he has set his heart on his servant Job) and in Pro 5:21 (the Lord weighs all a man's paths). The act is a looking at a person or a person's ways by the Lord, with Job as the object in the first two and the man's paths in the third.

Considering and counting as a done act appears in Neh 13:13 and 2Ch 9:20 (reckoned reliable, silver reckoned as nothing), Pro 17:28 (the silent fool counted wise), Heb 11:11, 11:19 and 11:26 (Sarah counting him faithful, Abraham concluding that God can raise the dead, Moses counting the reproach of Christ greater than treasures) and Mar 10:42 (those reputed to rule). The act is a judgment of standing or worth.

In 1Ki 10:21 the reckoning is negated: silver was not counted as anything in Solomon's days, and the negator reaches 'considered'. It is the only negated member of the group in the stored pairs that the negator reaches directly; in Jos 1:8, Eze 18:28, Mat 1:20 and Rom 4:19 the negators reach other verbs.
In 1Ki 10:21 the act is a refusal of worth: silver is counted as nothing, which the verse sets against the gold of Solomon's vessels.

Where the attending is of the law, God or his works it is a pursuit of its object: the love of the commandments comes within three words before the meditating in Psa 119:48 and Psa 119:97, and the psalmist's remembering stands 3 words before the meditating in Psa 63:6, Psa 77:3, Psa 77:6 and Psa 143:5. The attention is drawn toward what is loved or remembered.

The object of the meditating is the Lord's law and precepts in Jos 1:8, Psa 119:15, 119:27 and 119:78 (precepts 1 to 2 words from the member), his works and deeds in Psa 77:12, Psa 143:5 and Psa 145:5 (works 1 to 4 words), and the Lord himself and the days of old in Psa 63:6 and Psa 143:5. The object is God, what he has said and what he has done.

In Psa 38:12 the same verb of meditating has harm as its object: those who seek the speaker's hurt speak of ruin (1 word before) and meditate treachery, and in Psa 119:78 the speaker meditates on the precepts after he has been wronged (3 words before). The verb takes harm as its object in the first and is set against wrongdoing in the second.

The object of the considering is a person or the person's body in Job 1:8 and 2:3 (the servant Job), Rom 4:19 (Abraham's own body, as good as dead), Heb 11:11 (the one who promised), Eze 18:28 (the transgressions turned from), Ecc 2:11 (the work of his own hands) and Dan 7:8 (the horns). The objects are persons, bodies, deeds and the things seen in a vision.

The heart is named within three words of the member in five verses: 'the meditation of my heart' (Psa 19:14, Psa 49:3, each 1 word), 'in my heart' (Psa 77:6, 2 words), the heart of the righteous that ponders (Pro 15:28, 2 words before) and Mary pondering in her heart (Luk 2:19, 3 words). The verses place the attending in the heart.

Remembering stands exactly 3 words before the meditating in Psa 63:6, Psa 77:3, Psa 77:6 and Psa 143:5: the remembering of God, of a song or of the days of old comes first in the verse and the meditating follows it in the same sentence.

A second verb of musing stands in the same clause in Psa 77:12 (ponder, 3 before) and Psa 143:5 (ponder, 3 after), and the meditation of the heart is set between wisdom (1 before) and understanding (2 after) in Psa 49:3; in Pro 17:28 the silent fool is counted wise and intelligent. Wisdom and understanding stand beside the attending within four words in these verses.

Searching stands near the meditating in Psa 77:6 (search, 4 after, after the meditating), Psa 38:12 (seeking 7 and 4 before) and Act 10:19 (the men looking for Peter, 8 after the pondering). The search follows the attending in the first and the third and comes before it in the second.

Life and death are stated beside the considering in Eze 18:28 (the one who considers and turns away shall live, 8 after), Rom 4:19 (his body as good as dead, 4 after) and Heb 11:19 (raised from the dead, 7 after). In the last two what is considered is the state of death; in the first life is what follows the considering.

Fear and evil stand with the considering in Job 1:8 and Job 2:3 (the fear of God 9 to 10 words after, evil turned from 12 to 13 after), in Job 15:4 (fear of God and meditation both hindered, 2 words) and in Pro 15:28 (the wicked 3 words after the ponder). The attention of the Lord rests on one who fears God and turns from evil; the meditation is set beside what is done away with.

The nouns for meditation name the musing itself as a thing offered, loved or hindered: it is the meditation of the heart that is asked to be acceptable (Psa 19:14), that shall be understanding (Psa 49:3), that is asked to be pleasing (Psa 104:34), the law that is the speaker's meditation (Psa 119:97, Psa 119:99), and what is hindered before God (Job 15:4). Elijah's mockery names the god's musing (1Ki 18:27).

Weighing up as an evaluative act appears in Ecc 12:9, where the Preacher weighs proverbs with care and wisdom stands 6 words before; the physical weighing out of Ezr 8:29 is a counting of vessels before the priests. The evaluative weighing is one act of the attention of the Preacher among teaching, studying and arranging.

The surface 'weighing' is a weight in Gen 24:22 (twice), Jos 7:21 and Eze 5:1, a measure of shekels and not an act of the mind, and the surface 'weigh' is a physical weighing out in Ezr 8:29 and Zep 1:11 (laden); 'taking' stands beside the weights in the first three (took, 2 to 4 words). These occurrences are read as standalone: they are in the group because the surface also carries an evaluative use (1Cor 14:29, Ecc 12:9), and their placement was left as uncertain in the grouping.

The stored sense head of H6424 in Pro 5:21 reads 'to envy' against a lexicon range of weigh and make level (flagged in #2533), and the codes H0595 and H1934 in Pro 24:32 and Dan 7:8 are the pronoun I and a verb of being aligned into the units of 'considered'. They are not acts of attention; the verse acts are the verbs of setting the heart and contemplating beside them.

A thought is said within oneself and given as quoted speech in twenty-eight verses: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Saul, David, Naaman, Hezekiah and others each think something and the verse gives it. The code behind most is the verb 'to say', whose lexicon sense includes saying in one's heart; in several the thought is spoken to another in a dialogue.

A supposition is held about another person or a state of affairs and acted on, and in the verses of the Gospels and Acts it proves mistaken or unverified: Mary supposed to be going to the tomb, the gardener, the group on the journey, Paul dead, the prisoners escaped, a ghost, a spirit, a sleep, a purchase, a vision. In each the verb of thinking states the supposition and the verse then states what the people did or found.

A person holds a view of himself, which the verse then tests: that he is wise (1Cor 3:18), something (Gal 6:3), religious (Jam 1:26), a prophet (1Cor 14:37), standing (1Cor 10:12), with grounds for confidence (Phili 3:4), and that he knows (1Cor 8:2). The verb states a self-estimate, and the verse sets it beside deceiving oneself, folly or knowledge.

A thought is held as a purpose or plan in Num 33:56, 1Sa 18:25, 2Sa 21:16, 2Ch 13:8, 2Ch 32:1, Isa 10:7, Jer 23:27, Dan 7:25, Rut 4:4 and Phili 1:17: the Lord's purpose, Saul's snare, a giant's killing, withstanding a kingdom, conquering cities, destroying nations, making the people forget, changing the times, telling a kinsman and afflicting Paul. The verb is the same as for a supposition, and the verse gives the purpose within two words of it in several.

A view is asked of the hearer in eight verses, where Jesus or the writer puts the question and the hearer's opinion is what is sought: what do you think, Simon (Mat 17:25), a man with a hundred sheep (Mat 18:12), a man with two sons (Mat 21:28), is it lawful (Mat 22:17), what of the Christ (Mat 22:42), which of the three (Luk 10:36), the feast (Joh 11:56) and how much worse a punishment (Heb 10:29). The direction of the asking runs from the speaker to the hearer.

The supposition is forbidden, denied or withheld in twelve verses: do not think (Mat 5:17, Mat 10:34, Joh 5:45), we ought not to think (Act 17:29), that person must not suppose (Jam 1:7), let no one think me foolish (2Cor 11:16), let not my lord suppose (2Sa 13:32, 2Sa 13:33), not to think too highly (Rom 12:3, twice), do not think to yourself (Est 4:13), the heart does not so think (Isa 10:7) and no thought of her future (Lam 1:9). In each the negator reaches the member itself, one to seven words from it.

In these verses the act is a refusal as the grammar states it: Jesus rules out the supposition that he came to abolish the Law or bring peace, accuse you, or that God is like an image; Paul rules out thinking too highly of oneself and asks that no one think him foolish. The refusal is of a supposition about Jesus, about God or about oneself, and is spoken by Jesus, by Paul and by the one counselling.

Where the supposition is held and acted on the act is a pursuit of its content: the people follow Mary out, go a day's journey, stone Paul, draw the sword, sail on, send a gift, give a daughter to a snare. The thought is the ground of a move toward the thing supposed.

What is held to be so is dying or perishing in Gen 26:9, Job 29:18 and Jon 1:6 (the dying stands 2 words after the member and is the content of the thought), escaping in Gen 32:8, Est 4:13, Act 16:27 and Rom 2:3 (the escape is within ten words and is part of what is supposed), and someone's being dead in 2Sa 13:32, 2Sa 13:33 and Act 14:19.

What is held to be so is peace and security in 2Ki 20:19 and Isa 39:8 (Hezekiah's thought, security 3 to 4 words after) and in Mat 10:34 and Luk 12:51 (the supposition that Jesus came to bring peace, which is corrected); and fortified cities in 2Ch 32:1 and a guard in Jer 40:5. The same word peace is held by Hezekiah and denied of Jesus' coming.

What is held to be so is a state of the one who holds it: wise (1Cor 3:18, the wise within 2 words), religious (Jam 1:26), something when he is nothing (Gal 6:3), a prophet (1Cor 14:37), standing (1Cor 10:12), knowing (1Cor 8:2), with reason for confidence (Phili 3:4, confidence 6 before and 1 after) and thinking highly of oneself (Rom 12:3, faith 6 after). In each the object of the thinking is the thinker.

What is held to be so is another person's state or act: a prostitute (Gen 38:15, her face covered 2 words after), a gardener (Joh 20:15), in the group (Luk 2:44), drunk (Act 2:15), dead (Act 14:19), a sleep (Joh 11:13), a ghost (Mar 6:49), unclean (Rom 14:14, the uncleanness 2 words before) and not clean (1Sa 20:26). The object is a person or a thing in a state the speaker has not verified.

What is thought of is the steadfast love of the Lord in Psa 48:9 (1 word after the member), and what answers the thought of falling is the same steadfast love in Psa 94:18 (3 words after); the poor are the ones the Lord thinks of in Psa 40:17 (poor 3 before, needy 2 before) and the ones the unworthy thought turns from in Deu 15:9 (poor 10 after). The thinking is directed at the Lord's love or at the poor.

The outward act that follows a supposition is stated in the same verse: the Jews follow Mary (Joh 11:31, going 2 words after), Joseph's people go a day's journey (Luk 2:44), the crowds stone Paul (Act 14:19), the jailer draws his sword (Act 16:27, killing 2 words before), the sailors weigh anchor (Act 27:13), Saul gives his daughter as a snare (1Sa 18:21, give 1 after), and Jacob sends a present (Gen 32:20, present 3 after). The supposition and the act it leads to stand in the one sentence.

A supposition issues in a spoken answer or a question in the exchanges of Gen 18:29 to 18:32, Gen 31:31, Exo 2:14, Est 4:13, Luk 7:43 and Luk 13:2: the supposition is put in the speaker's own words as part of a dialogue, with 'answered' 1 to 13 words from the member.

Fear stands within three words before the thought in Gen 31:31, Exo 2:14, 2Sa 14:15 and Neh 6:9, in Luk 24:37 (startled and frightened, 3 and 1 words before) and in Gen 20:11 (the fear of God, 3 words after). In five of the six the fear is named before the thought and the thought comes from it.

Anger, hiding and hunger stand beside the thought in Gen 18:30 and Gen 18:32 (the Lord's anger), 2Ki 5:11 (Naaman's anger, 4 words before), Psa 64:5 (secretly, 1 word before), 2Ki 7:12 (hide, 2 words before; hungry, 6 before) and Gen 38:15 (the covering of her face, 2 words after). The thought arises in a person who is angry, hiding or hungry, or who is faced with something concealed.

Affliction, suffering and crying stand with the thought in Lam 1:9 (affliction), 1Cor 7:26 (the present distress, 3 words after), Phili 1:17 (afflict, 1 after), 1Pe 4:1 (Christ suffered, within 2 words), Luk 13:2 (suffered), Mar 6:49 (cried out, 4 after), Joh 11:31 and Joh 20:15 (weeping) and Deu 15:9 (the cry to the Lord, 14 after). The thinking is set in verses of distress or of a response to it.

The heart or the mind is named with the thought in Deu 15:9 and 2Sa 13:33 (1 word), Isa 10:7 (2 words), Eze 20:32 and Rom 1:21 (3 words), 1Ch 28:9, Mat 9:4 and 1Ti 6:5 (4 words), Eze 11:5 (6) and Jam 1:26 (10). The verses place the thought in the heart or mind of the one who holds it.

Knowing stands with the thought in thirteen verses: in 1Cor 8:2 knowledge is 1 word after the member and is what the person thinks he has, in Ecc 9:10 knowledge is 1 word after and is stated as absent in Sheol, in Mat 9:4 and Eze 11:5 the thinking is known by another, and in Act 12:9 and Rom 1:21 knowing is stated as lacking or as turned to futile thinking. The thought is set beside knowledge, held, lacking or known by another.

Trust, loyalty and silence stand with the thought in 1Sa 27:12 (Achish trusted David, 2 words before), 2Ki 18:20 and Isa 36:5 (whom do you trust, 8 after), Mic 2:8 (trustingly, 1 before), Psa 48:9 and Psa 94:18 (steadfast love within 3 words) and Psa 50:21 (silence 1 word before the false supposition). Trust is the ground of Achish's thought, and the Lord's silence is the ground of the supposition that he is like the one who has done these things.

Asking and calling stand with the supposition in Mat 6:7 (those who pray suppose they will be heard), Mat 26:53 (the supposition whether Jesus cannot appeal), 2Sa 14:15 (the request the woman came to make), 2Ki 5:11 (Naaman supposes the prophet will call on the name of the Lord, 4 after), Jer 3:19 (call me Father, 1 after) and Jon 1:6 (call out to your god, 4 before the hope). The supposition is about being heard or about a call.

Searching and finding stand with the supposition in Gen 18:28 and Gen 18:30 ('find' is the condition of each supposed number), Mat 18:12, Luk 2:44 and Joh 20:15 (the search follows the supposition or the question) and Joh 5:39 (searching the Scriptures, 4 words before the supposition). The supposition is set in a verse of a search or of a condition to be found.

Sin, judging and evil stand with the supposition in Luk 13:2 (worse sinners), Eze 18:14 (a son who sees his father's sins), Rom 2:3 (you who judge), Joh 5:45 (accuse), Mat 9:4 (evil, 1 word after), Psa 64:5 (evil, 5 before), 1Cor 14:20 (evil, 2 before) and Pro 21:29 (the wicked, 5 before). In Mat 9:4 the evil is what is thought; in the others it stands in the clause of the person who thinks.

Believing, honor, reward and the commandment stand with the thought in Pro 14:15 (the simple believes, 3 words before), Rom 12:3 (faith, 6 after), Jam 1:26 (religion, 12 after), 2Sa 10:3 and 1Ch 19:3 (honoring, 4 after), 1Cor 12:23 (honor, 3 after), Heb 10:29 (punishment, 1 before), Mat 22:17 (pay, 2 after) and Num 36:6 and 1Cor 14:37 (the Lord's command). In each the thought is about something owed, believed or commanded.

Truth, righteousness and the lawful stand with the supposition in Job 35:2 (just, 2 after), Mat 22:17 (lawful, 1 after), 2Cor 12:6 (truth, 5 before), 1Ti 6:5 (truth, 1 before), Phili 4:8 (honorable and just, 13 to 15 before) and Gen 18:28 (the righteous in the case put). The thought is a judgment whether something is right, true or lawful.

War, return and the endurance of a held position stand with the thought in 2Ki 18:20 and Isa 36:5 (war, 5 after), 1Sa 18:17 (fight and battles), Mic 2:8 (war, 1 after), Jer 3:7 (return, 5 after, expected and not done), Heb 11:15 (return, 8 after, what thinking of the land would have allowed), 2Ch 13:8 (withstand, 1 after) and 1Cor 7:26 (remain, 9 after). The thought is of conflict, of return or of holding out.

Small words stand in the units of the surfaces of this group and do not carry the sense of supposing: the connective G1161 in 1Cor 8:2, Rom 2:3 and 2Pe 1:13, G2532 in Rom 1:21, the particles and pronouns H3588A (Gen 20:11), H1931 (Pro 21:29), H0834A (Eze 20:32), H0853 (Neh 6:9), the preposition H0413 (Jer 40:4), the copula H1961 (Deu 15:9) and the returning H7725G (Mic 2:8). They are read in their verses as standalone and were read at stage 1 for what they do.

In the verses of the quoted thought the partner collections hold words that are not words of their collection's meaning: the surface 'surely' stands as a member of 'hear' in Exo 2:14, Jdg 3:24, 1Sa 16:6, 1Sa 20:26 and 2Ki 5:11; 'unworthy' as a member of 'reward' in Deu 15:9; 'presence' and 'present' as members of 'offer' in Rut 4:4 and 1Cor 7:26; and 'will' as a member of 'desire' in 2Sa 14:17 and 2Ki 7:12. These are recorded as open item #2536 and are not resolved here.

Thoughts come out of or arise in a person: evil thoughts come out of the heart in Mat 15:19 and Mar 7:21 (the heart 3 to 4 words before, the thoughts the first of the things named), thoughts will come into the mind in Eze 38:10, and thoughts came to the king on his bed in Dan 2:29. The act is the arising of a thought in the heart or mind, and in the first two it issues in the acts that the verses list after it.

Another knows, perceives or discerns the thoughts: Job knows his friends' thoughts (Job 21:27), the Lord knows the thoughts of man (Psa 94:11), you discern my thoughts (Psa 139:2), Jesus knows or perceives theirs (Mat 9:4, Mat 12:25, Luk 5:22, Luk 6:8, Luk 11:17), the Lord knows what the wise think and finds it futile (1Cor 3:20), the Spirit knows a person's (1Cor 2:11) and the word of God discerns them (Heb 4:12). The verb of knowing stands within four words before the member in most of the verses where its position is stored.

The thoughts alarm the one who has them in Dan 4:19, Dan 5:6, Dan 5:10 and Dan 7:28: the thoughts are the subject of the alarming, the verb stands 1 to 2 words after the member, and the change of color is named within five words. The act runs from the thoughts to the person.

An opinion is declared in Job 32:6, 32:10 and 32:17 (Elihu says he will declare his opinion, the declaring 2 words before) and laid bare in Pro 18:2 (the fool takes pleasure in expressing his heart). The opinion is a view held and then spoken, in the first three in an answer within a dialogue.

The Lord's own thoughts are stated as done and known by those who hear: his thoughts toward us are multiplied (Psa 40:5), very deep (Psa 92:5), precious (Psa 139:17), higher than ours (Isa 55:8, Isa 55:9) and not known by the nations (Mic 4:12, plan 4 words after). The Lord's thoughts are named beside his works in Psa 92:5 and Isa 66:18.

Evil and iniquitous thoughts are held or planned in Gen 6:5, Job 21:27, Psa 56:5, Pro 15:26, Isa 55:7, Isa 59:7, Jer 4:14 and Psa 10:4, with 'evil' or 'wicked' within five words of the member in each. The thoughts are of the wicked and the verses name the thought and the evil together.

A thought is asked to be searched and known in Psa 139:23 (search me and know my thoughts, the knowing 2 words before) and a person is told to forsake his thoughts in Isa 55:7 (the unrighteous man his thoughts, 5 words after the wicked). The first is asked of God and the second is said by the Lord of a person.

The thoughts are not known, not the same, not cared about: the nations do not know what the Lord thinks (Mic 4:12, the negator 2 words before the member), the Lord's thoughts are not our thoughts (Isa 55:8), and you do not care about anyone's opinion (Mat 22:16, Mar 12:14, the negator reaches 'care'). In each the thought or opinion is the object of a negated knowing, sameness or care.

Where the thoughts of persons are given up, set against God's or left uncared for, the act is a refusal as the verses state it: the unrighteous man is to forsake his thoughts (Isa 55:7) and the opinion of persons is not regarded (Mat 22:16, Mar 12:14). Where the psalmist asks to be known the act is a pursuit.
Where the psalmist asks that his thoughts be known and tried (Psa 139:23) and speaks of the Lord's thoughts as precious (Psa 139:17) the act is a pursuit of what is asked or valued.

The thoughts are of iniquity in Isa 59:7, of evil in Gen 6:5, against the speaker in Psa 56:5, the words 'there is no God' in Psa 10:4, the wicked's in Pro 15:26 and the righteous's in Pro 12:5 (just), toward us in Psa 40:5 and of the Lord in Mic 4:12; the opinion in Mat 22:16 and Mar 12:14 is of persons and what they appear to be. The object or content of the thought is named in the verse or set beside the word within three words.

The evil thoughts come out of the heart together with the acts the verses list after them: sexual immorality 1 to 3 words after the member in Mat 15:19 and Mar 7:21, with murder, adultery, theft, false witness and slander in the same list. The thought is the first of the things that come out and the acts follow it in the same sentence.

A heart or mind is named with the thoughts in all fifteen verses of the pairing: within three words in Gen 6:5, 1Ch 29:18, Dan 2:30, Luk 1:51, Eze 38:10, Mat 15:19, Luk 2:35 and Heb 4:12, and 4 to 9 away in Psa 139:23, Mar 7:21, Jer 4:14, Mat 9:4, Luk 5:22 and Dan 7:28; in Rom 2:15 the conscience stands 3 words before. The thoughts are placed in the heart, mind or conscience of the person.

Wealth, teaching and counsel stand with the thought in a few verses: the imagination is the wall of the rich man's wealth (Pro 18:11, wealth 6 before), the thoughts are not to be cursed in even against the rich (Ecc 10:20, rich 7 after), the counsels of the wicked stand beside the thoughts of the righteous (Pro 12:5, 3 after), and the opinion of persons is set against teaching the way of God (Mat 22:16, Mar 12:14). The thought is set beside the wealth, the counsel or the teaching of the one who holds it.

Qualifiers of the thoughts are 'evil' directly before the noun in Mat 15:19, Mar 7:21 and Jam 2:4 (1 word before), 'wicked' in Jer 4:14 (1 before), 'very deep' in Psa 92:5 and 'of the righteous' and 'of the wicked' in Pro 12:5 and Pro 15:26. The adjective gives the thought its moral character in the verses of evil and its depth in the verse of the Lord's thoughts.

Codes of the surfaces of this group have senses of their own that differ from 'thought': H8312 in Psa 139:23 (stored sense head 'anxiety'), H5587B in Job 20:2 (disquietings), H1902H in Lam 3:62 (the muttered musing of enemies), H1697I in Eze 38:10 (matters that come up), G0991 in Mat 22:16 and Mar 12:14 (a looking at persons, not an opinion held) and G3588 in 1Cor 2:11 (the article, morph empty, flagged in #2533). They are recorded as they stand in their verses.

Conceiving is foreseen as an announcement in Jdg 13:3, 13:5 and 13:7, Isa 7:14, Mat 1:23 and Luk 1:31 (you shall conceive and bear a son), made by the angel of the Lord, by the Lord or by an angel to a woman, and as a condition in Num 5:28 (a clean woman shall conceive). The act stands in the future and is paired with bearing a son in each of the announcements.

Conceiving is a done act in Psa 51:5 (the speaker's mother conceived him) and in Heb 11:11 (Sarah received power to conceive); in the Greek verse the conceiving is carried by a phrase of two nouns, 'laying down' and 'seed', and in Mat 1:23 by the verb 'to have' with 'in'. The act is bodily and is stated of a woman in each verse.

The figurative conceiving of what is then borne is a done act in Job 15:35 (trouble conceived and evil borne), Isa 33:11 (chaff conceived and stubble borne) and Isa 59:4 (mischief conceived and iniquity borne). The same code H2029 whose Poel sense is to contrive or devise is used of bodily conceiving in Jdg 13:3; in these three verses what is conceived is evil and what is borne is evil or stubble.

In Num 11:12 the conceiving is put as a rhetorical question: Moses asks whether he conceived all this people and gave them birth. The question presupposes that he did not, so the conceiving is stated as not done by him and the bodily word is used of his relation to the people.

Devising harm is a done act in Psa 41:7: those who hate the speaker whisper together and imagine the worst for him. The verb is the code H2803I whose lexicon sense is to plan or devise, and the unit also holds the preposition H5921A, 'upon', beside it.
The devising of Psa 41:7 is a pursuit of harm: the object is the worst for the speaker, and the verb is set among whispering and hating.
In Num 11:12 the act is a refusal as the question puts it: Moses denies having conceived the people and so denies the charge laid on him.

What is conceived is a son in Jdg 13:5, 13:7, Isa 7:14, Mat 1:23 and Luk 1:31, children in Num 5:28, the speaker in Psa 51:5, a people in Num 11:12, trouble, chaff and mischief in Job 15:35, Isa 33:11 and Isa 59:4, and the worst against the speaker in Psa 41:7. The conceiving of a child is the commoner object across the verses.

Bearing follows the conceiving in six verses: 1 word after the member in Jdg 13:3, 13:5, 13:7 and Isa 7:14, 2 after in Mat 1:23 and 4 after in Luk 1:31; and calling the child's name follows in Isa 7:14 (3 after), Mat 1:23 (5) and Luk 1:31 (7). The conceiving is the first act of a pair or a series, bearing and naming.

The conceiving is stated of women whose condition the verse names: barren and not having borne (Jdg 13:3), clean and not defiled (Num 5:28), and in Heb 11:11 Sarah past the age; the negators of these verses reach the words defiled and borne, and in Jdg 13:5 and 13:7 they reach what the woman must not do (a razor, wine, unclean food). The conceiving is announced under a condition of the woman.

The divine and the human are named in eight verses: God (4), the Lord and Jesus, with Immanuel (3), Sarah (2), the woman and the child. The messenger or the Lord announces the conceiving to the woman, the woman conceives and bears a son, and the child is called by the name the Lord gives; the direction of the announcement does not change across the verses.

Small words stand in the units of the surfaces of this group and do not carry the sense of conceiving or devising: the preposition H5921A in Psa 41:7, the Greek 'in' (G1722) in Mat 1:23 and the verb 'to have' (G2192) read with it, which together form the idiom rendered conceive. They are read in their verses as standalone beside the member that gives the sense; the grouping placed the whole surface 'conceive' under devising although most of its occurrences are bodily conceiving, which was left as uncertain.

Behaviour discovered: holding a supposition about another person or a state of affairs, and answering or acting on it. The elements show a thought quoted to oneself or a supposition held (22506, 22507), its content stated (death, escape, peace, security, another's state, the Lord's love: 22514, 22515, 22517), the act or the spoken answer that follows it in the same verse (22513, 22519, 22520), and the circumstances that stand beside it: fear, anger, hiding, distress, knowing, trust, asking, searching, sin, truth and war (22521 to 22523, 22525 to 22529, 22531, 22532). They belong together because each is a part of one working: a supposition formed and then lived out. This gathers the elements named by the traced observations and states no claim about what the behaviour is.

Behaviour discovered: holding a view of oneself that the verse then tests. The elements show a person thinking he is wise, something, religious, a prophet, standing or knowing (22508), the object of the thinking being the thinker (22516), and the believing, honor, reward and commanding that stand beside it (22530). They belong together because the supposition is about the holder and the verse sets it beside deceiving oneself, folly or knowledge. This gathers the elements named by the traced observations and states no claim about what the behaviour is.

Behaviour discovered: putting a view to a hearer, and ruling a supposition out. The elements show the view of the hearer asked for (22510), the supposition forbidden or denied by Jesus, Paul and others (22511) and the act stated as a refusal (22512). They belong together because the asking and the ruling out both address a supposition held or to be held by the hearer, and the direction runs from the speaker to the hearer. This gathers the elements named by the traced observations and states no claim about what the behaviour is.

Behaviour discovered: devising or purposing harm, or a course against another. The elements show a thought held as a purpose or plan (22509), the devising of Psa 41:7 and its pursuit of harm (22555, 22556), the meditating on treachery of Psa 38:12 (22494), evil and iniquitous thoughts planned or held (22540, 22545) and the figurative conceiving of trouble and mischief that is then borne (22553). They belong together because in each the mind forms something against another before it is carried out, across the supposing, attending, thoughts and devising subgroups. This gathers the elements named by the traced observations and states no claim about what the behaviour is.

Behaviour discovered: meditating on God, his word and his works. The elements show musing on a named matter and pondering (22485), the resolve to meditate on precepts, statutes and works (22486), the command of Jos 1:8 (22487), the pursuit of what is loved or remembered (22492), the object being the law, God's works and God himself (22493), the heart as place and remembering as what comes first (22496, 22497), a second verb of musing in the same clause (22498), searching near it (22499), the nouns for the meditation itself (22502) and the thought on the Lord's steadfast love of Psa 48:9 (22518). They belong together because each is a going over of God, what he has said or what he has done. This gathers the elements named by the traced observations and states no claim about what the behaviour is.

Behaviour discovered: the Lord considering persons and knowing their thoughts. The elements show the Lord asking whether Satan has set his heart on Job and weighing a man's paths (22488), the fear of God and evil turned from that stand beside the considering (22501), another knowing, perceiving or discerning thoughts (22536) and Jesus knowing the reasoning in the disciples' hearts (22474). They belong together because in each the knower or considerer is God, Jesus or the Spirit and the object is a person or a person's thoughts. This gathers the elements named by the traced observations and states no claim about what the behaviour is.

Behaviour discovered: considering a matter and drawing a conclusion from it. The elements show the object of the considering as a person, a body, a deed or a vision (22495), life and death stated beside it (22500) and the counting that issues in a conclusion in Heb 11 (22489). They belong together because the considering is followed in the verse by what is concluded or what follows from it. This gathers the elements named by the traced observations and states no claim about what the behaviour is.

Behaviour discovered: reckoning or counting a person or thing as something, and the standing given. The elements show the counting as a done act (22489), a negated act in 1Ki 10:21 and its refusal of worth (22490, 22491), the counting foreseen (22461) and the complement that names the standing: foreigners, a strange thing, the greatest (22467). They belong together because each assigns a standing or worth to the thing counted, in the attending and the taking-account subgroups. This gathers the elements named by the traced observations and states no claim about what the behaviour is.

Behaviour discovered: giving or withholding regard to a person or thing. The elements show regard given (22460), asked of God (22462), withheld in thirteen verses (22463, 22464), the pursuit (22465), the objects regarded (22466), the negator that turns the act into a denial (22468), the worth or conceit of the one regarded (22469), contempt in the same sentence (22470) and hearing paired with regard (22471). They belong together because each is a taking account of someone or something, given or denied, by persons and by God. This gathers the elements named by the traced observations and states no claim about what the behaviour is.

Behaviour discovered: reasoning with others from grounds to persuade. The elements show reasoning as a done act of speech in the Acts verses (22473), the child's reckoning of 1Cor 13:11 (22475), what the reasoning is on (22476), the qualifiers of its length and manner (22482) and the directions in which it runs (22483). They belong together because each is an exchange of grounds put to hearers. This gathers the elements named by the traced observations and states no claim about what the behaviour is.

Behaviour discovered: stating or denying the ground of an act or a state. The elements show the ground named by 'for this reason' and 'the reason why' (22477), set beside bearing and sin (22478), knowing stated as the ground of error (22479), the ground denied (22480) and the denial as a refusal (22481). They belong together because each names, or withholds, what an act or state rests on. This gathers the elements named by the traced observations and states no claim about what the behaviour is.

Behaviour discovered: setting the mind on an object, against an opposite. The elements are the whole of the subgroup: the setting of the mind done, stated as a mind-set and negated (22452 to 22454), its pursuit and refusal (22455, 22456), the object as one of a pair of opposites (22457) and the circumstance of a way of living and its issue and of a rebuke (22458, 22459). They belong together because every element concerns the direction of the mind toward the flesh or the Spirit, God or man. This gathers the elements named by the traced observations and states no claim about what the behaviour is.

Behaviour discovered: thoughts that arise in a person, are known by another, and issue in acts or are declared. The elements show thoughts coming out of the heart and the acts listed after them (22535, 22546), the heart or mind as their place (22547), the moral character given to them by qualifiers (22549), knowing, perceiving and discerning by another (22536, 22541), the thoughts not known or not the same as the Lord's (22542, 22543), the pursuit of being known (22544), thoughts alarming the one who has them (22537), the opinion declared (22538), the Lord's thoughts (22539), the content of thoughts (22545) and their setting beside wealth and counsel (22548). They belong together because each concerns a thought as a thing held in a person, which another knows or which comes out. This gathers the elements named by the traced observations and states no claim about what the behaviour is.

Behaviour discovered: weighing up what is said or taught. The elements show the command to the others to weigh what the prophets say (22487) and the Preacher weighing proverbs with care (22503). They belong together because in both the weighing is an evaluation of words spoken or taught. This gathers the elements named by the traced observations and states no claim about what the behaviour is.

The heart or the mind is named as the place of the working in three subgroups: of the attending (the meditation of the heart, the heart of the righteous that ponders, Mary pondering in her heart), of the supposing (the heart or mind named with the thought within three words in several verses) and of the thoughts (all fifteen verses of the pairing). The heart is the place stated in each, across the elements of three subgroups.

Knowing stands beside the working in three subgroups: knowledge as what the supposer thinks he has or lacks (22525), the knowing of Mar 12:24 as the ground of error (22479) and the knowing of another as the way thoughts are held (22536). In the first the one who thinks is the knower, in the second the lack of knowing is the ground, and in the third another knows the thoughts.

Fear and alarm stand with the working in three subgroups: fear within three words before the supposition (22521), the fear of God that describes the one the Lord considers (22501) and the thoughts that alarm (22537). The fear precedes the supposition, accompanies the one considered and is caused by the thoughts, according to the verses of each.

The working appears in a negated form in each of five subgroups: the supposition forbidden (22511), regard withheld (22463), the setting of the mind negated (22454), the reckoning negated in 1Ki 10:21 (22490), the ground denied (22480) and thoughts not known (22542). In each the negator reaches the member in the verses named, and the denial is stated beside what is affirmed in the opposite verses.

God, the Lord and Jesus stand as the one who knows, considers, regards or corrects in several subgroups: the Lord considering Job and weighing paths (22488), knowing thoughts (22536), Jesus rebuking Peter (22459), the Lord regarded or not regarded (22466) and the correction of a supposition by Jesus (22511). The divine entity is the knower, the object or the one who corrects, and the direction differs by subgroup.

Anger and the supposition meet in three verses. In Gen 18:30 and Gen 18:32 the Lord's anger is what Abraham asks not to be roused, 2 and 4 words before the supposed number, and the supposition is the case he puts while the anger is held back; in 2Ki 5:11 Naaman's own anger stands 4 words before his quoted thought. The anger is the setting of the supposition, the Lord's in the first two and the thinker's in the third.

Believing and the supposition meet in four verses with different ties. In Pro 14:15 the simple believes everything 3 words before the prudent gives thought, and the two are set against each other; in Rom 12:3, Phili 3:4 and Jam 1:26 the faith, confidence or religion is the thing the person thinks of himself, 1 to 12 words from the member. The supposition is about one's own standing in belief.

Blessing words stand far from the supposition in three verses: grace 11 words before in Rom 12:3, a willing gift 16 words after in 2Cor 9:5 and grace 16 after in Heb 10:29. At these distances the partner is in another clause, and the two work together only in that the same verse speaks of what is given and of what is thought of oneself or others; no tie of grammar joins them.

Calling and the supposition meet in four verses. In 2Ki 5:11 (4 words after) and Jer 3:19 (1 after) the call is what the thinker expected would be made; in Jon 1:6 the command to call on his god stands 4 words before the hope that the god will give thought to them; in Gen 26:9 the calling of Isaac is 12 words before and is a separate act. The call is the expected or commanded act that the supposition concerns.

War and the supposition meet in four verses: in 2Ki 18:20 and Isa 36:5 war stands 5 words after the thought that words are strategy and power for it, in Mic 2:8 it is 1 word after the thought of the passersby, and in 1Sa 18:17 fight and battles stand 4 and 2 words before Saul's quoted thought. Conflict is what the supposed strength or the plan is for.

Comfort and the supposition meet in three verses with different relations. In Psa 119:52 the thinking of the Lord's rules and the comfort taken are in one clause, comfort 4 words after; in Job 12:5 the at-ease (1 word after the thought) hold contempt for misfortune; in Joh 11:31 the consoling stands 10 words before the supposition that explains why they followed Mary out.

Commanding and the supposition meet in five verses. In Num 36:6 the Lord's commands stand 4 words before the thought of whom they think best; in 1Cor 14:37 the command (11 words after) is what the one who thinks he is a prophet is to acknowledge; in Psa 50:21 the charge (2 after) follows the false supposition about God; in Rom 12:3 and 2Sa 13:32 the partner is 8 and 12 words after, in later clauses. The supposition is set against a command or charge.

Concealing and the supposition meet in three verses: the covering of her face (2 words after) is the ground of Judah's supposition in Gen 38:15; hiding (2 before) and secretly (1 before) stand beside the quoted thoughts of the Syrians and of the wicked in 2Ki 7:12 and Psa 64:5. The thought is formed from, or alongside, something concealed.

Judging and the supposition meet in four verses. In Joh 5:45 (accuse, 3 after) and Rom 2:3 (judge, 3 after) the supposition concerns accusation or judgment; in Luk 7:43 the judging (8 after) is the answer given to Simon's supposition; in Exo 2:14 'judge' is 8 words before, in the question the accuser puts to Moses. The supposition and the judging are set side by side in each.

Persuading and the supposition meet in three verses: persuaded stands 8 words before the supposition of the crowds in Act 14:19 and 13 before Paul's thought of the unclean in Rom 14:14, and obeying stands 3 words after the thought taken captive in 2Cor 10:5. The persuasion is a separate earlier act in the first two, and the obedience is the end of the thought in the third.

Deceiving and the supposition meet in three verses: 6 words before in 1Cor 3:18, 5 after in Gal 6:3 and 8 after in Jam 1:26.
